# Windows Optimization & Debloat Tools – Complete Feature Reference

_Compiled 2026-10-11. Covers 17 programs: what every feature/tweak does at the technical level (registry keys and values, services, scheduled tasks, commands, scripts)._

## How this document was built
- **Open-source tools** (WinUtil, Win11Debloat, Winhance, Sophia Script, Sparkle, AtlasOS, ReviOS + Revision Tool, Bulk Crap Uninstaller, RemoveWindowsAI, CrapFixer, Flyoobe) were documented **directly from their source code / config files** (JSON, `.reg`, YAML playbooks, C#/PowerShell/Dart definitions). Registry tables and command blocks are machine-extracted from the code; command blocks list the state-changing lines of each script (logging/UI lines omitted). Repository snapshots used:
  - WinUtil: `ChrisTitusTech/winutil` @ 07ccd8e 2026-10-07
  - Win11Debloat: `Raphire/Win11Debloat` @ 17e0661 2026-10-08
  - Winhance: `memstechtips/Winhance` @ db80ecf 2026-09-30
  - Sophia Script: `farag2/Sophia-Script-for-Windows` @ a2f03d8 2026-10-11
  - Sparkle: `parcoil/sparkle` @ c4f5b88 2026-10-10
  - AtlasOS: `Atlas-OS/Atlas` @ 1ed9630 2026-05-04
  - ReviOS playbook: `meetrevision/playbook` @ 3c2c973 2026-10-09
  - Revision Tool: `meetrevision/revision-tool` @ 386dd51 2026-10-11
  - Bulk Crap Uninstaller: `Klocman/Bulk-Crap-Uninstaller` @ 30da609 2026-09-08
  - RemoveWindowsAI: `zoicware/RemoveWindowsAI` @ 23a6af6 2026-10-10
  - CrapFixer: `builtbybel/CrapFixer` @ 58e280a 2026-10-08
  - Flyoobe: `builtbybel/Flyoobe` @ 3ea0acf 2026-10-08
- **Closed-source tools** (O&O ShutUp10++, Winaero Tweaker, Autoruns, Process Lasso, NVCleanstall, DDU) were documented from official documentation, release notes and developer statements. Where a vendor does not publish the exact registry write, the document names the **Microsoft-documented setting behind the feature** and says so.
- **Legend:** `HKLM`/`HKCU`/`HKCR`/`HKU` = registry hives; `∅` (Winhance) = value deleted; service start types 0 Boot, 1 System, 2 Automatic, 3 Manual, 4 Disabled; “Undo/OFF” columns show what the tool writes when reverting.
- Tools change over time; re-check the linked repositories before relying on a specific value. Many tweaks (disabling Defender, mitigations, updates, VBS, UAC) reduce security – they are documented here, not recommended.

## 1. Chris Titus Tech WinUtil
**Type:** PowerShell/WPF all-in-one utility (install apps, tweaks, Windows features, fixes, update policy, Windows ISO creator). **Source:** https://github.com/ChrisTitusTech/winutil (MIT). **Launch:** `irm "https://christitus.com/win" | iex` (stable) or `irm "https://christitus.com/windev" | iex` (dev). All data below is extracted from `config/tweaks.json`, `config/feature.json`, `config/appx.json`, `config/dns.json`, `config/preset.json`, `config/applications.json` and the `functions/` folder of the repository (commit snapshot Oct 2026).
**How tweaks are applied (engine):** each tweak entry can contain `registry` (written with `Set-WinUtilRegistry`, i.e. `New-Item`/`Set-ItemProperty` with the given type; `<RemoveEntry>` as original value means *undo deletes the value*), `service` (`Set-WinUtilService` → `Set-Service -StartupType`), `ScheduledTask` (enable/disable), `InvokeScript` (PowerShell run as admin) and `UndoScript`. Toggles (“Customize Preferences”) write `Value` when switched ON and `OriginalValue` when switched OFF; the toggle state is read back from the registry. The “Undo Selected Tweaks” button writes every `OriginalValue`, restores `OriginalType` for services and runs `UndoScript`. Explorer is restarted after Explorer-related changes.
### 1.1 Tweaks tab
Total entries in `tweaks.json`: **67**.
**Presets:**
- **Standard**: `WPFTweaksActivity`, `WPFTweaksConsumerFeatures`, `WPFTweaksDisableExplorerAutoDiscovery`, `WPFTweaksWPBT`, `WPFTweaksLocation`, `WPFTweaksServices`, `WPFTweaksTelemetry`, `WPFTweaksDeliveryOptimization`, `WPFTweaksDiskCleanup`, `WPFTweaksDeleteTempFiles`, `WPFTweaksEndTaskOnTaskbar`, `WPFTweaksRestorePoint`
- **Minimal**: `WPFTweaksConsumerFeatures`, `WPFTweaksWPBT`, `WPFTweaksServices`, `WPFTweaksTelemetry`
- **Advanced**: `WPFTweaksRestorePoint`, `WPFTweaksActivity`, `WPFTweaksConsumerFeatures`, `WPFTweaksDisableExplorerAutoDiscovery`, `WPFTweaksWPBT`, `WPFTweaksLocation`, `WPFTweaksServices`, `WPFTweaksTelemetry`, `WPFTweaksDeliveryOptimization`, `WPFTweaksDeleteTempFiles`, `WPFTweaksEndTaskOnTaskbar`, `WPFTweaksDisableStoreSearch`, `WPFTweaksRevertStartMenu`, `WPFTweaksWidget`, `WPFTweaksRemoveOneDrive`, `WPFTweaksWindowsAI`, `WPFTweaksRightClickMenu`
- **AppxDefault**: `WPFAppxMicrosoft_WindowsFeedbackHub`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_GetHelp`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_MicrosoftOfficeHub`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_WindowsCalculator`, `WPFAppxClipchamp_Clipchamp`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_WindowsAlarms`, `WPFAppxMicrosoftCorporationII_QuickAssist`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_WindowsSoundRecorder`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_MicrosoftStickyNotes`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_Todos`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_MicrosoftSolitaireCollection`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_PowerAutomateDesktop`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_WindowsDevHome`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_BingWeather`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_StartExperiencesApp`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_BingNews`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_Copilot`, `WPFAppxMicrosoft_BingSearch`

#### Essential Tweaks
##### Activity History - Disable  
`WPFTweaksActivity` · type: CheckBox

> Stops Windows from publishing or uploading user activities while preserving clipboard history.

| Registry key | Value name | Type | Applied value | Undo value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System | EnableActivityFeed | DWord | 1 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System | PublishUserActivities | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System | UploadUserActivities | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |

##### Hibernation - Disable  
`WPFTweaksHiber` · type: CheckBox

> Hibernation is really meant for laptops as it saves what's in memory before turning the PC off. It really should never be used.

| Registry key | Value name | Type | Applied value | Undo value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Power | HibernateEnabled | DWord | 0 | 1 |
| HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\FlyoutMenuSettings | ShowHibernateOption | DWord | 0 | 1 |

Script executed:

```powershell
powercfg.exe /hibernate off
```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
powercfg.exe /hibernate on
```


</details>

##### Widgets - Remove  
`WPFTweaksWidget` · type: CheckBox

> Removes the annoying widgets in the bottom left of the Taskbar.

Script executed:

```powershell
# Sometimes if you dont stop the Widgets process the removal may fail

Get-Process *Widget* | Stop-Process
Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.WidgetsPlatformRuntime -AllUsers | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers
Get-AppxPackage MicrosoftWindows.Client.WebExperience -AllUsers | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers

Invoke-WinUtilExplorerUpdate -action "restart"
Write-Host "Removed widgets"

```

`WPFTweaksRevertStartMenu` · type: CheckBox

> Bring back the old Start Menu layout from before the gradual rollout of the new one in 25H2. On newer versions of Windows !!THIS TWEAK WILL NOT WORK!!

| Registry key | Value name | Type | Applied value | Undo value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\3036241548 | EnabledState | DWord | 1 | <RemoveEntry> |

##### Services - Set to Manual  
`WPFTweaksServices` · type: CheckBox

> Sets some services to Manual startup and adjusts the SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB registry value to better match system memory, which can significantly reduce the number of svchost.exe processes.

Services:

| Service | Startup type set | Original (undo) |
|---|---|---|
| CscService | Disabled | Manual |
| DiagTrack | Disabled | Automatic |
| MapsBroker | Manual | Automatic |
| StorSvc | Manual | Automatic |
| SharedAccess | Disabled | Automatic |

Script executed:

```powershell
$Memory = (Get-CimInstance Win32_PhysicalMemory | Measure-Object Capacity -Sum).Sum / 1KB
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control" -Name SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB -Value $Memory

```

##### Telemetry - Disable  
`WPFTweaksTelemetry` · type: CheckBox

> Disables Microsoft Telemetry.

| Registry key | Value name | Type | Applied value | Undo value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AdvertisingInfo | Enabled | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Privacy | TailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticDataEnabled | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Speech_OneCore\Settings\OnlineSpeechPrivacy | HasAccepted | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Input\TIPC | Enabled | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization | RestrictImplicitInkCollection | DWord | 1 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization | RestrictImplicitTextCollection | DWord | 1 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization\TrainedDataStore | HarvestContacts | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Personalization\Settings | AcceptedPrivacyPolicy | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\DataCollection | AllowTelemetry | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced | Start_TrackProgs | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System | PublishUserActivities | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |
| HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Siuf\Rules | NumberOfSIUFInPeriod | DWord | 0 | <RemoveEntry> |

Script executed:

```powershell
# Disable Defender Auto Sample Submission
Set-MpPreference -SubmitSamplesConsent 2

# Disable (Connected User Experiences and Telemetry) Service
Set-Service -Name diagtrack -StartupType Disabled

# Disable (Windows Error Reporting Manager) Service
Set-Service -Name wermgr -StartupType Disabled

# Disable PowerShell 7 telemetry
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('POWERSHELL_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT', '1', 'Machine')

Remove-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Siuf\Rules" -Name PeriodInNanoSeconds

```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
# Enable Defender Auto Sample Submission
Set-MpPreference -SubmitSamplesConsent 1

# Enable (Connected User Experiences and Telemetry) Service
Set-Service -Name diagtrack -StartupType Automatic

# Enable (Windows Error Reporting Manager) Service
Set-Service -Name wermgr -StartupType Automatic

# Enable PowerShell 7 telemetry
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('POWERSHELL_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT', '', 'Machine')

```


</details>

`WPFTweaksDiskCleanup` · type: CheckBox

> Runs Disk Cleanup on Drive C: and removes old Windows Updates.

Script executed:

```powershell
Dism.exe /online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup /ResetBase

```

##### Temporary Files - Remove  
`WPFTweaksDeleteTempFiles` · type: CheckBox

> Erases TEMP Folders.

Script executed:

```powershell
# A temp folder always holds files something has open, including this run's own, and
# the job layer counts a logged error as a failed step
Remove-Item -Path "$Env:Temp\*" -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item -Path "$Env:SystemRoot\Temp\*" -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

```

##### File Explorer Automatic Folder Discovery - Disable  
`WPFTweaksDisableExplorerAutoDiscovery` · type: CheckBox

> Windows Explorer automatically tries to guess the type of the folder based on its contents, slowing down the browsing experience. WARNING! Will disable File Explorer grouping.

Script executed:

```powershell
# Previously detected folders
$bags = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags"

# Folder types lookup table
$bagMRU = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU"

# Flush Explorer view database
Remove-Item -Path $bags -Recurse -Force
Write-Host "Removed $bags"

Remove-Item -Path $bagMRU -Recurse -Force
Write-Host "Removed $bagMRU"

# Every folder
$allFolders = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags\AllFolders\Shell"

if (!(Test-Path $allFolders)) {
  New-Item -Path $allFolders -Force
  Write-Host "Created $allFolders"
}

# Generic view
New-ItemProperty -Path $allFolders -Name "FolderType" -Value "NotSpecified" -PropertyType String -Force
Write-Host "Set FolderType to NotSpecified"

Write-Host Please sign out and back in, or restart your computer to apply the changes!

```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
# Previously detected folders
$bags = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags"

# Folder types lookup table
$bagMRU = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU"

# Flush Explorer view database
Remove-Item -Path $bags -Recurse -Force
Write-Host "Removed $bags"

Remove-Item -Path $bagMRU -Recurse -Force
Write-Host "Removed $bagMRU"

Write-Host Please sign out and back in, or restart your computer to apply the changes!

```


</details>

#### Advanced Tweaks – CAUTION

##### Microsoft Edge - Remove  
`WPFTweaksRemoveEdge` · type: CheckBox

> Uninstalls Microsoft Edge by creating dummy MicrosoftEdge.exe file in the legacy Edge folder. This tricks Windows into unlocking the official Edge uninstaller allowing for a system-level removal.

Script executed:

```powershell
$Path = Resolve-Path -Path "$Env:ProgramFiles (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\*\Installer\setup.exe" | Select-Object -Last 1

if (Test-Path $Path) {
    New-Item -Path "$Env:SystemRoot\SystemApps\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge_8wekyb3d8bbwe\MicrosoftEdge.exe" -Force
    Start-Process -FilePath $Path -ArgumentList "--uninstall --system-level --force-uninstall --delete-profile" -Wait
    Write-Host "Microsoft Edge was removed"
} else {
    Write-Host "Microsoft Edge is not installed"
}

```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
Write-Host "Installing Microsoft Edge..."
winget install Microsoft.Edge --source winget

```


</details>

##### Microsoft OneDrive - Remove  
`WPFTweaksRemoveOneDrive` · type: CheckBox

> Denies permission to remove OneDrive user files, then uses its own uninstaller to remove it and restores the original permission afterward.

Script executed:

```powershell
# Deny permission to remove OneDrive folder
icacls $Env:OneDrive /deny "*S-1-5-32-544:(D,DC)"

Write-Host "Uninstalling OneDrive..."
Start-Process -FilePath (Join-Path $Env:SystemRoot "System32\OneDriveSetup.exe") -ArgumentList '/uninstall' -Wait

# Some of OneDrive files use explorer, and OneDrive uses FileCoAuth
Write-Host "Removing leftover OneDrive Files..."

Stop-Process -Name FileCoAuth,Explorer

Remove-Item "$Env:LocalAppData\Microsoft\OneDrive" -Recurse -Force
Remove-Item "$Env:ProgramData\Microsoft OneDrive" -Recurse -Force

# Grant back permission to access OneDrive folder
icacls $Env:OneDrive /grant "*S-1-5-32-544:(D,DC)"

if (-not (Get-ChildItem -Path $Env:OneDrive)) {
    Remove-Item -Path $Env:OneDrive -Recurse
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('OneDrive', $null, 'User')
}

# Disable OneSyncSvc
Set-Service -Name OneSyncSvc -StartupType Disabled

```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
Write-Host "Installing OneDrive"
winget install Microsoft.Onedrive --source winget

# Enabled OneSyncSvc
Set-Service -Name OneSyncSvc -StartupType Automatic

```


</details>

##### DNS - Set to:  
`WPFchangedns` · type: Combobox

Options: `Default`, `DHCP`, `Fastest`, `Google`, `Cloudflare`, `Cloudflare_Malware`, `Cloudflare_Malware_Adult`, `Open_DNS`, `Quad9`, `AdGuard_Ads_Trackers`, `AdGuard_Ads_Trackers_Malware_Adult`. `Default` = no change, `DHCP` = reset to automatic (`Set-DnsClientServerAddress -ResetServerAddresses`), `Fastest` = runs the built-in DNS benchmark (`Get-WinUtilDNSBenchmark`, measures resolve latency of every provider flagged `BenchmarkEligible`) and applies the winner.

| Provider | IPv4 primary | IPv4 secondary | IPv6 primary | IPv6 secondary | DoH template |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google | 8.8.8.8 | 8.8.4.4 | 2001:4860:4860::8888 | 2001:4860:4860::8844 | https://dns.google/dns-query |
| Cloudflare | 1.1.1.1 | 1.0.0.1 | 2606:4700:4700::1111 | 2606:4700:4700::1001 | https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query |
| Cloudflare_Malware | 1.1.1.2 | 1.0.0.2 | 2606:4700:4700::1112 | 2606:4700:4700::1002 | https://security.cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query |
| Cloudflare_Malware_Adult | 1.1.1.3 | 1.0.0.3 | 2606:4700:4700::1113 | 2606:4700:4700::1003 | https://family.cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query |
| Open_DNS | 208.67.222.222 | 208.67.220.220 | 2620:119:35::35 | 2620:119:53::53 | https://doh.opendns.com/dns-query |
| Quad9 | 9.9.9.9 | 149.112.112.112 | 2620:fe::fe | 2620:fe::9 | https://dns.quad9.net/dns-query |
| AdGuard_Ads_Trackers | 94.140.14.14 | 94.140.15.15 | 2a10:50c0::ad1:ff | 2a10:50c0::ad2:ff | https://dns.adguard-dns.com/dns-query |
| AdGuard_Ads_Trackers_Malware_Adult | 94.140.14.15 | 94.140.15.16 | 2a10:50c0::bad1:ff | 2a10:50c0::bad2:ff | https://family.adguard-dns.com/dns-query |

Implementation (`Set-WinUtilDNS`) – key operations:

```powershell
Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $Adapter.ifIndex -ResetServerAddresses
netsh interface ip set dnsservers name="$($Adapter.Name)" source=dhcp
netsh interface ipv6 set dnsservers name="$($Adapter.Name)" source=dhcp
Remove-Item -Path $dohInterfaceSettings -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Set-DnsClientDohServerAddress -ServerAddress $ip -DohTemplate $dohTemplate -AllowFallbackToUdp $false -AutoUpgrade $true -ErrorAction Stop
New-Item -Path $regPath -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
New-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name "DohFlags" -Value 1 -PropertyType QWord -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $Adapter.ifIndex -ServerAddresses $ipv4Addresses -ErrorAction Stop
Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $Adapter.ifIndex -ServerAddresses $ipv6Addresses -ErrorAction Stop
```

### 1.3 Install tab (application installer)
Installs/uninstalls/upgrades programs with **WinGet** (default) or **Chocolatey** (radio switch). WinGet is (re)installed if missing via `Install-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -Force; Install-Module Microsoft.WinGet.Client -Force; Repair-WinGetPackageManager -AllUsers`. Commands used (one call per package): install `winget install --id <id> --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements --source winget|msstore --silent`; upgrade `winget upgrade --id <id> ... --include-unknown --silent` or `winget upgrade --all --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements --include-unknown --silent`; uninstall `winget uninstall --id <id> --source <src> --silent`; Chocolatey: `choco install|upgrade|uninstall <id> -y --no-progress` (Chocolatey itself is installed by `Install-WinUtilChoco` if missing). Other buttons: **Get Installed** (marks already-installed apps), **Show selected apps**, **Clear selection**, **FOSS-only filter**, category chips, search. Selections can be exported/imported as JSON (`Invoke-WPFImpex`) and replayed headless with the script parameters `-Config <file.json>` and/or `-Preset <Standard|Minimal|Advanced>` (`Invoke-WinUtilAutoRun`); `-Offline` skips online lookups.

### 1.5 Win11 ISO creator (formerly MicroWin)
Takes an official Windows ISO, lets you pick the edition, optionally injects drivers exported from the current PC (storage/`SCSIAdapter`/`HDC` class drivers also go into `boot.wim` index 2) and writes an `autounattend.xml` (generated with the schneegans.de unattend generator schema) plus `sources\ei.cfg` for the chosen edition. The install image itself is not debloated; instead a first-logon script `C:\Windows\Setup\Scripts\WinUtil-PostInstall.ps1` is embedded and executed from `FirstLogon.ps1`. Output: a new ISO (built with `oscdimg`) or written directly to USB (`Invoke-WinUtilISOUSB`: `diskpart clean` on the selected disk, creates a partition, `Format-Volume -FileSystem FAT32`, copies the media; large `install.wim` handled by the script). The embedded post-install script does exactly this:

Provisioned AppX packages removed: `Clipchamp.Clipchamp`, `Microsoft.BingNews`, `Microsoft.BingSearch`, `Microsoft.BingWeather`, `Microsoft.GetHelp`, `Microsoft.MicrosoftOfficeHub`, `Microsoft.MicrosoftSolitaireCollection`, `Microsoft.MicrosoftStickyNotes`, `Microsoft.OutlookForWindows`, `Microsoft.Paint`, `Microsoft.PowerAutomateDesktop`, `Microsoft.StartExperiencesApp`, `Microsoft.Todos`, `Microsoft.Windows.DevHome`, `Microsoft.WindowsFeedbackHub`, `Microsoft.WindowsSoundRecorder`, `Microsoft.ZuneMusic`, `MicrosoftCorporationII.QuickAssist`, `MSTeams`

```powershell
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ReserveManager' 'ShippedWithReserves' 'REG_DWORD' '0'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\BitLocker' 'PreventDeviceEncryption' 'REG_DWORD' '1'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Chat' 'ChatIcon' 'REG_DWORD' '3'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection' 'AllowTelemetry' 'REG_DWORD' '0'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\dmwappushservice' 'Start' 'REG_DWORD' '4'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsCopilot' 'TurnOffWindowsCopilot' 'REG_DWORD' '1'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge' 'HubsSidebarEnabled' 'REG_DWORD' '0'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer' 'DisableSearchBoxSuggestions' 'REG_DWORD' '1'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Teams' 'DisableInstallation' 'REG_DWORD' '1'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Mail' 'PreventRun' 'REG_DWORD' '1'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent' 'DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures' 'REG_DWORD' '1'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent' 'DisableConsumerAccountStateContent' 'REG_DWORD' '1'
Set-WinUtilRegistryValue 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent' 'DisableCloudOptimizedContent' 'REG_DWORD' '1'
```

### 1.6 Other functions
- **Create Restore Point** before tweaks (Essential tweak `WPFTweaksRestorePoint`, see above).
- **Environment report export** (`Invoke-WPFExportEnvironmentReport`): collects OS build, hardware, installed apps, applied tweak state and recent WinUtil logs into a zip for support.
- **Import/Export** of all selections (`Invoke-WPFImpex`) and headless automation via `-Config` / `-Preset` (see Install tab).
- **Themes**: light/dark/auto UI theme, font scaling (`Invoke-WinUtilFontScaling`).
- **Logging**: per-run logs in the WinUtil folder `logs` subdirectory (fallback `%LOCALAPPDATA%\winutil\logs`).

---

## 2. Win11Debloat (Raphire)
**Type:** PowerShell script with WPF GUI + CLI. **Source:** https://github.com/Raphire/Win11Debloat (MIT). **Launch:** `& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm "https://debloat.raphi.re/")))` (optionally followed by parameters). Every feature is a script parameter of the same name (e.g. `-DisableTelemetry -RemoveApps -Silent`). Control parameters: `-Silent` (no prompts), `-RunDefaults`, `-RunDefaultsLite`, `-RunSavedSettings`, `-Sysprep` (apply to the Default user profile so new accounts inherit the changes), `-User <name>` (apply to another user's hive, loaded with `reg load`), `-NoRestartExplorer`, `-CreateRestorePoint`, `-SkipRegistryBackup`, `-WhatIf`, `-LogPath`, `-Apps "<comma list>"`, `-AppRemovalTarget`. Before applying registry features it exports a **registry backup** (snapshot of every value it will touch, restorable from the GUI “Restore backup” dialog). Registry features are applied by importing `.reg` files from `Regfiles\` (`reg import`; for other users/Sysprep the hive path is rewritten to the loaded hive). Each feature has an Undo `.reg` file (`Regfiles\Undo\`). Data below comes from `Config/Features.json`, `Config/Apps.json`, `Config/DefaultSettings.json`, all `.reg` files and `Scripts/` (Oct 2026).

**Default mode (`-RunDefaults`) enables:** `CreateRestorePoint`, `DisableAISvcAutoStart`, `DisableBing`, `DisableClickToDo`, `DisableCopilot`, `DisableDragTray`, `DisableEdgeAds`, `DisableLockscreenTips`, `DisableModernStandbyNetworking`, `DisableRecall`, `DisableStoreSearchSuggestions`, `DisableSuggestions`, `DisableTelemetry`, `DisableWidgets`, `Hide3dObjects`, `HideChat`, `ShowKnownFileExt` (+ removal of the default app selection).

### 2.1 Features
#### General / app removal / special
##### Remove the apps specified with the 'Apps' parameter  
`-RemoveApps`

Removes the selected apps (see app catalogue below). AppX apps: `Get-AppxPackage` → `Remove-AppxPackage` (current user, or `-AllUsers` when target = all users; for all users also `Remove-ProvisionedAppxPackage -Online -AllUsers` so they are not reinstalled for new accounts). Apps with RemovalMethod `Winget` are removed with `winget uninstall --accept-source-agreements --disable-interactivity --id <id>` (if that fails at the time it is scheduled via a RunOnce entry).

##### Remove the Xbox App and Xbox Gamebar  
`-RemoveGamingApps`

Removes AppX packages `Microsoft.GamingApp`, `Microsoft.XboxGameOverlay`, `Microsoft.XboxGamingOverlay` (Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers | Remove-AppxPackage + Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage).

##### Remove HP OEM applications  
`-RemoveHPApps`

Removes HP OEM AppX packages: `AD2F1837.HPAIExperienceCenter`, `HPJumpStarts`, `HPPCHardwareDiagnosticsWindows`, `HPPowerManager`, `HPPrivacySettings`, `HPSupportAssistant`, `HPSureShieldAI`, `HPSystemInformation`, `HPQuickDrop`, `HPWorkWell`, `myHP`, `HPDesktopSupportUtilities`, `HPQuickTouch`, `HPEasyClean`, `HPConnectedMusic`, `HPFileViewer`, `HPRegistration`, `HPWelcome`, `HPConnectedPhotopoweredbySnapfish`, `HPPrinterControl` (all prefixed `AD2F1837.`).

##### Create a system restore point  
`-CreateRestorePoint` · **on by default**

If System Restore is off it runs `Enable-ComputerRestore -Drive $env:SystemDrive`; if no restore point exists from the last 24 h it runs `Checkpoint-Computer -Description "Restore point created by Win11Debloat" -RestorePointType MODIFY_SETTINGS`.

##### Replace the start menu layout for this user only with the provided template file  
`-ReplaceStart` · min build 22621

Replaces `start2.bin` of the current/target user with a user-supplied `start2.bin` template (`-ReplaceStart <path>`).

##### Replace the start menu layout for all existing and new users with the provided template file  
`-ReplaceStartAllUsers` · min build 22621

Same as ReplaceStart for all users + default profile.

##### Forcefully uninstall Microsoft Edge. NOT RECOMMENDED!  
`-ForceRemoveEdge`

Forced Edge uninstall: creates `HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdateDev` value `AllowUninstall` = "" (32-bit view), creates a stub folder `%SystemRoot%\SystemApps\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge_8wekyb3d8bbwe\MicrosoftEdge.exe`, reads `UninstallString` from `HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\Microsoft Edge` and runs it with `--force-uninstall`, then deletes Edge shortcuts (Start menu, Quick Launch, taskbar pins, Public/User desktop), the stub folder and the autostart values `MicrosoftEdgeAutoLaunch_*` / `Microsoft Edge Update` in `HKCU\...\Run` and `...\Explorer\StartupApproved\Run`.

If you are a Windows Insider, updates may be blocked until optional diagnostic data collection is turned back on.

| SET | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced` | `LaunchTo` | REG_DWORD | `3` |

Undo: `Launch_File_Explorer_To_Home.reg` (“Change the default location that File Explorer opens to 'Home'”).

##### Change the default location that File Explorer opens to 'OneDrive'  
`-ExplorerToOneDrive`

Part of option group “Open File Explorer to” → choice “OneDrive”.

Registry file `Launch_File_Explorer_To_OneDrive.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced` | `LaunchTo` | REG_DWORD | `4` |

Undo: `Launch_File_Explorer_To_Home.reg` (“Change the default location that File Explorer opens to 'Home'”).

##### Show drive letters before drive label  
`-ShowDriveLettersFirst`

Part of option group “Drive letter position” → choice “Show drive letters before drive label”.

> This setting will show drive letters before the drive label in File Explorer.

Registry file `Show_Drive_Letters_First.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer` | `ShowDriveLettersFirst` | REG_DWORD | `4` |

Undo: `Show_Drive_Letters_Last.reg` (“Show drive letters after drive label”).

##### Show drive letters after drive label  
`-ShowDriveLettersLast`

Part of option group “Drive letter position” → choice “Show drive letters after drive label (Default)”.

> This setting will show drive letters after the drive label in File Explorer (Default Windows behavior).

Registry file `Show_Drive_Letters_Last.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer` | `ShowDriveLettersFirst` | REG_DWORD | `0` |

##### Show network drive letters before drive label  
`-ShowNetworkDriveLettersFirst`

Part of option group “Drive letter position” → choice “Show network drive letters before drive label”.

> This setting will show only network drive letters before the drive label in File Explorer.

Registry file `Show_Network_Drive_Letters_First.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer` | `ShowDriveLettersFirst` | REG_DWORD | `1` |

Undo: `Show_Drive_Letters_Last.reg` (“Show drive letters after drive label”).

##### Hide all drive letters  
`-HideDriveLetters`

Part of option group “Drive letter position” → choice “Hide all drive letters”.

> This setting will hide all drive letters from the File Explorer navigation pane and 'This PC'.

Registry file `Hide_Drive_Letters.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer` | `ShowDriveLettersFirst` | REG_DWORD | `2` |

Undo: `Show_Drive_Letters_Last.reg` (“Show drive letters after drive label”).

#### Windows Update
##### Prevent getting updates as soon as they're available  
`-DisableUpdateASAP`

> This will prevent your PC from being among the first to receive new non-security updates. Your PC will still receive these updates eventually.

Registry file `Disable_Update_ASAP.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings` | `IsContinuousInnovationOptedIn` | REG_DWORD | `0` |

Undo: `Enable_Update_ASAP.reg` (“Allow getting updates as soon as they're available”).

##### Prevent automatic restarts after updates while signed in  
`-PreventUpdateAutoReboot`

> This will prevent your PC from automatically restarting after updates while any user is signed in.

Registry file `Prevent_Auto_Reboot.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU` | `NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers` | REG_DWORD | `1` |

Undo: `Allow_Auto_Reboot.reg` (“Allow automatic restarts after updates while signed in”).

##### Disable sharing downloaded updates with other PCs  
`-DisableDeliveryOptimization`

> This will prevent your PC from sharing downloaded updates with other PCs on the local network or on the internet. This also prevents your PC from downloading updates from other PCs.

Registry file `Disable_Delivery_Optimization.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKU\S-1-5-20\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\DeliveryOptimization\Settings` | `DownloadMode` | REG_DWORD | `0` |

Undo: `Enable_Delivery_Optimization.reg` (“Enable sharing downloaded updates with other PCs”).

##### Prevent Windows from auto-installing device companion apps  
`-DisableDeviceAutoAppDownload`

> Stops Windows from silently installing device companion apps via Windows Update when you connect certain devices, like monitors from LG and Alienware. These devices will still work as expected, this only stops Windows Update from automatically installing additional apps without consent.

Registry file `Disable_Device_Auto_App_Download.reg`:

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Device Metadata` | `PreventDeviceMetadataFromNetwork` | REG_DWORD | `1` |

Undo: `Enable_Device_Auto_App_Download.reg` (“Allow automatic installation of device companion apps”).

#### Optional Windows Features
##### Enable Windows Sandbox  
`-EnableWindowsSandbox` · min build 22483

> Windows Sandbox is a lightweight desktop environment for safely running applications in isolation. Software installed inside the Windows Sandbox environment remains 'sandboxed' and runs separately from the host machine. Only supported on Windows 11 Pro, Workstation, and Enterprise editions.

`Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Containers-DisposableClientVM -All -NoRestart` (undo: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature).

##### Enable Windows Subsystem for Linux  
`-EnableWindowsSubsystemForLinux` · min build 22000

> Windows Subsystem for Linux allows you to run a Linux environment directly on Windows without the need for a virtual machine.

Enables optional features `VirtualMachinePlatform` and `Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux` (undo disables both).

## 3. O&O ShutUp10++
**Type:** closed-source privacy configurator (Free portable edition + Premium edition with background service), Windows 10/11; current series 3.x. **Vendor:** O&O Software GmbH, https://www.oo-software.com/shutup10, manual https://manuals.oo-software.com/ooshutup10/. **How it works (per the official manual):** almost 300 settings in 20+ categories, each a registry or Group Policy value. Two tabs – **Current User** (HKCU) and **Local Machine** (HKLM); where both exist, the machine value wins and the app offers to align the user value (“Linked system/user setting” dialog). Only settings that exist on the installed Windows version/edition are shown. After every write the value is read back; if Windows/Group Policy blocks it, the real cause is reported. Each setting has a recommendation level (Recommended / Limited / Not recommended); the **Actions** menu applies all Recommended, Recommended + Limited, or all settings, and offers “Undo all changes” (restore Windows defaults) and a System Restore point. Changes are recorded per session and can be undone step by step. Settings can be exported/imported as `.cfg` (`ID<TAB>+/-`), also unattended: `OOSU10.exe <file.cfg> /quiet`. Premium adds a service that re-applies chosen settings after Windows updates, profiles, and no-admin operation; newer versions also include an AI-feature removal function.

> **Registry column:** O&O does not publish the exact value each switch writes and the app is closed source. The column shows the **Microsoft-documented policy/registry value that controls that setting** (the same values used by the open-source tools above). Treat it as the equivalent mechanism, not as a dump of ShutUp10’s binary. Empty = no single documented value could be assigned with confidence.

---

## 4. Winhance
**Type:** native C# desktop app (.NET 10, WinUI 3), installer + portable. **Source:** https://github.com/memstechtips/Winhance (MIT). Every setting is a `SettingDefinition` record in `src/Winhance.Core/Features/*/Models/*.cs`; the generic engine (`SettingApplicationService`) writes the listed registry values (ON → first `EnabledValue`, OFF → first `DisabledValue`; `∅` means the value is deleted), runs the attached PowerShell scripts, imports `.reg` content, sets power settings through `powercfg`/native power APIs, and enables/disables scheduled tasks. Current state is detected by reading the same values (so the UI shows the live state). Badges show “Recommended” and “Windows default”. Settings flagged `RequiresAdvancedUnlock` are hidden behind an advanced/expert unlock. Global features: system restore point before changes, configuration export/import (`.winhance` config files), “Quick Actions” (apply all recommended / reset all to Windows default per feature or globally), change history, light/dark theme, multi-language UI.

PowerShell when ON:

```powershell
Get-NetAdapter | ForEach-Object { Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $_.InterfaceIndex -ServerAddresses @('{{primary}}','{{secondary}}') }
```


PowerShell when OFF:

```powershell
Get-NetAdapter | ForEach-Object { Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $_.InterfaceIndex -ResetServerAddresses }
```


PowerShell when ON:

```powershell
$known = @('1.1.1.1','1.0.0.1','8.8.8.8','8.8.4.4','9.9.9.9','149.112.112.112'); foreach ($s in $known) { netsh dns delete encryption server=$s 2>$null | Out-Null }; $t = '{{dohtemplate}}'; if ($t -and $t -notmatch '^\{\{') { netsh dns add encryption server={{primary}} dohtemplate=$t autoupgrade=yes udpfallback=no | Out-Null; netsh dns add encryption server={{secondary}} dohtemplate=$t autoupgrade=yes udpfallback=no | Out-Null }
```


PowerShell when OFF:

```powershell
$known = @('1.1.1.1','1.0.0.1','8.8.8.8','8.8.4.4','9.9.9.9','149.112.112.112'); foreach ($s in $known) { netsh dns delete encryption server=$s 2>$null | Out-Null }
```

| HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard | Locked | DWord | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |  |

```powershell
null
```

### 4.8 Customize → Start Menu (13 settings)
##### Clean Start Menu  
`SettingIds.StartMenuCleanWin10` · Action · RequiresConfirmation

> Removes all pinned items and applies a clean layout for the current user and any newly created profiles. To clean other existing users, run this again while signed in as each of them.

PowerShell when ON:

```powershell
$layoutPath = 'C:\Users\Default\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\LayoutModification.xml'
$layoutXml = @'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<LayoutModificationTemplate xmlns:defaultlayout="http://schemas.microsoft.com/Start/2014/FullDefaultLayout" xmlns:start="http://schemas.microsoft.com/Start/2014/StartLayout" Version="1" xmlns:taskbar="http://schemas.microsoft.com/Start/2014/TaskbarLayout" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/Start/2014/LayoutModification">
    <LayoutOptions StartTileGroupCellWidth="6" />
    <DefaultLayoutOverride>
        <StartLayoutCollection>
            <defaultlayout:StartLayout GroupCellWidth="6" />
        </StartLayoutCollection>
    </DefaultLayoutOverride>
</LayoutModificationTemplate>
'@

# Future users: drop the clean template into the Default profile (force-create dir, overwrite if present).
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Split-Path $layoutPath) -Force | Out-Null
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($layoutPath, $layoutXml)

# Current user only: apply now via their SID (HKU, not HKCU - correct under OTS), then unlock so they can still customize.
# Other existing users are intentionally not touched - Win10 has no supported way to apply a
# customizable layout to a signed-out profile, so users re-run this per account (see description).
$me = ((Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).UserName -split '\\')[-1]
if ($me) {
    $sid = (New-Object System.Security.Principal.NTAccount($me)).Translate([System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier]).Value
    $key = "HKU\$sid\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer"
    reg add $key /v StartLayoutFile /t REG_SZ /d $layoutPath /f | Out-Null
    reg add $key /v LockedStartLayout /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f | Out-Null
    Stop-Process -Name StartMenuExperienceHost -Force -EA SilentlyContinue; Start-Sleep 3
    reg add $key /v LockedStartLayout /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f | Out-Null
    Stop-Process -Name StartMenuExperienceHost -Force -EA SilentlyContinue
}
```


PowerShell when OFF:

```powershell
null
```


##### Clean Start Menu  
`SettingIds.StartMenuCleanWin11` · Action · RequiresConfirmation

> Removes all pinned items and applies clean layout

| Key | Value | Type | ON | OFF | Recommended | Win default | Policy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\PolicyManager\current\device\Start | ConfigureStartPins | String | {"pinnedList":[]} | ∅ (absent/delete) | {"pinnedList":[]} | ∅ (absent/delete) |  |
| HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer | ConfigureStartPins | String | {"pinnedList":[]} | ∅ (absent/delete) | {"pinnedList":[]} | ∅ (absent/delete) | GPO |

PowerShell when ON:

```powershell
# Clear cached pinned-list data (start.bin / start2.bin) for every real user profile.
# Iterating HKLM\ProfileList is OTS-safe and admin can delete in any profile, so the
# current user and every other user are handled in one loop. ProfileImagePath gives
# the correct path even for non-default profile locations (e.g. D:\Users\...).
$systemAccounts = @('Public','Default','All Users','Default User')
Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList' |
    Where-Object { $_.PSChildName -like 'S-1-5-21-*' } |
    ForEach-Object {
        $profilePath = (Get-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name 'ProfileImagePath' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ProfileImagePath
        if ($profilePath -and ((Split-Path $profilePath -Leaf) -notin $systemAccounts)) {
            Remove-Item "$profilePath\AppData\Local\Packages\Microsoft.Windows.StartMenuExperienceHost_cw5n1h2txyewy\LocalState\start*.bin" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        }
    }

# Restart the Start Menu host so the cleared layout takes effect immediately.
Stop-Process -Name 'StartMenuExperienceHost' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```


PowerShell when OFF:

```powershell
null
```

### 4.11 Power plans
The “Power Plan” setting (first entry of the Power group above) lists all installed schemes plus predefined ones. Selecting a predefined plan creates it if missing: **Winhance Power Plan** = `powercfg /duplicatescheme 381b4222-f694-41f0-9685-ff5bb260df2e <fixed GUID>` (duplicate of Balanced, renamed, then every recommended power setting from 4.3 is applied to it); **Ultimate Performance** = native `PowerDuplicateScheme` of the hidden scheme `e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61` and renamed; other predefined plans (Balanced/High performance/Power saver) are restored from their GUIDs. The plan is activated with `PowerSetActiveScheme`/`powercfg /setactive`. All per-setting changes in 4.3 are written to the active plan for AC and DC.

### 4.12 Software & Apps – Windows apps, capabilities, optional features
Removal runs a generated script `C:\ProgramData\Winhance\Scripts\BloatRemoval.ps1` (from `BloatRemovalScriptGenerator`) which does: `Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -PackageName <pkg>`, `Remove-AppxPackage -Package <pkg> -AllUsers`, `Remove-WindowsCapability -Online -Name <cap>`, `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName <f> -NoRestart`, stops related processes, and for Xbox Game Bar re-points the `ms-gamebar`/`ms-gamebarservices` URL protocols to `systray.exe` (prevents the “you need an app to open ms-gamebar” popup) and sets `AppCaptureEnabled=0`, `GameDVR_Enabled=0`, policy `AllowGameDVR=0`. The script is also registered as a **scheduled task** (runs at startup/logon as SYSTEM, highest privileges) so removed apps are removed again if Windows Update reinstalls them. Removed apps can be reinstalled (Store ID via winget/msstore, capabilities via `Add-WindowsCapability`, features via `Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature`). Special removal scripts exist for **Edge** (`EdgeRemovalScript.cs`) and **OneDrive** (`OneDriveRemovalScript.cs`).

**EdgeRemovalScript** – key operations:

````powershell
Start-Process PowerShell.exe -ArgumentList ("-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File `"{0}`"" -f $PSCommandPath) -Verb RunAs
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $logFolder -Force | Out-Null
Remove-Item $logFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
"$timestamp - Log rotated - previous log exceeded 500KB" | Out-File -FilePath $logFile
"$timestamp - $Message" | Out-File -FilePath $logFile -Append
$packageInfo = & dism /online /Get-PackageInfo /PackageName:$package 2>$null
Stop-Process -Name $_ -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Set-ItemProperty -Path $packagePath -Name "Visibility" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (Test-Path $ownersPath) { Remove-Item -Path $ownersPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
$dismProcess = Start-Process -FilePath "dism.exe" -ArgumentList "/online", "/Remove-Package", "/PackageName:$edgeLegacyPackageVersion" -NoNewWindow -PassThru
$retryProcess = Start-Process -FilePath "dism.exe" -ArgumentList "/online", "/Remove-Package", "/PackageName:$edgeLegacyPackageVersion" -NoNewWindow -PassThru
Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
Remove-Item -Path $path -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $scriptsDir -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
$openWebSearchContent | Out-File -FilePath $openWebSearchPath -Encoding ASCII -Force
reg.exe add "HKCR\microsoft-edge" /f /ve /d "URL:microsoft-edge" 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe add "HKCR\microsoft-edge" /f /v "URL Protocol" /d `"`" 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe add "HKCR\microsoft-edge" /f /v "NoOpenWith" /d `"`" 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe add "HKCR\microsoft-edge\shell\open\command" /f /ve /d "$stubTargetPath %1" 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\ie_to_edge_stub.exe" /f /v UseFilter /d 1 /t reg_dword 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\ie_to_edge_stub.exe\0" /f /v FilterFullPath /d "$stubTargetPath" 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\ie_to_edge_stub.exe\0" /f /v Debugger /d "$conhostDebugger" 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe delete "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\msedge.exe" /f 2>&1 | Out-Null

reg.exe add "HKCR\MSEdgeHTM\shell\open\command" /f /ve /d "```"`$stubPath```" %1" 2>&1 | Out-Null
$repairContent | Out-File -FilePath $repairScriptPath -Encoding UTF8 -Force
$repairAction = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "powershell.exe" -Argument "-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -Command `"iex([IO.File]::ReadAllText('$repairScriptPath'))`""
$repairTrigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogon
$repairSettings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries -StartWhenAvailable
$repairPrincipal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "SYSTEM" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $repairTaskName -TaskPath "\Winhance\" -Action $repairAction -Trigger $repairTrigger -Settings $repairSettings -Principal $repairPrincipal -Force | Out-Null
New-Item -Path $edgePath -ItemType Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
New-Item -Path $edgePath -ItemType File -Name "MicrosoftEdge.exe" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
if ($uninstallString -like "*msiexec*") {
Start-Process cmd.exe "/c $uninstallString /quiet" -WindowStyle Hidden -Wait | Out-Null
Start-Process cmd.exe "/c $uninstallString --force-uninstall --silent" -WindowStyle Hidden -Wait | Out-Null
Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge.Stable | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $edgePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
Start-Process -FilePath $path -ArgumentList "/unregsvc" -Wait -WindowStyle Hidden -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Start-Process -FilePath $path -ArgumentList "/uninstall" -Wait -WindowStyle Hidden -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
cmd /c "reg import `"$backupRegFile`"" 2>$null
Remove-Item $backupRegFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item $path -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $item.Path -Name $item.Name -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item $key.PSPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $muiCachePath -Name $prop.Name -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item $edgeLocalPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Copy-Item $stubPath "$scriptsDir\ie_to_edge_stub.exe" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$edgeFolders | Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
reg.exe add "HKCR\MSEdgeHTM\shell\open\command" /f /ve /d """`"$stubPath`""" %1" 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe delete "HKCR\MSEdgeHTM" /f 2>&1 | Out-Null
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName $task.TaskName -TaskPath $task.TaskPath -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
````

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $logFolder -Force | Out-Null
Remove-Item $logFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
"$timestamp - Log rotated - previous log exceeded 500KB" | Out-File -FilePath $logFile
"$timestamp - $Message" | Out-File -FilePath $logFile -Append
Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers *OneDriveSync* | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Stop-Process -Name "*OneDrive*" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
Start-Process -FilePath $exePath -ArgumentList $arguments -WindowStyle Hidden -Wait | Out-Null
reg.exe delete $hklmUninstallKey /f 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe delete $uninstallKey /f 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe delete $path /f 2>&1 | Out-Null
takeown /f $currentUserOneDrivePath /r /d y 2>&1 | Out-Null
icacls $currentUserOneDrivePath /grant "${env:USERNAME}:F" /t 2>&1 | Out-Null
Remove-Item $currentUserOneDrivePath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item $startMenuPath -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\OneDrive.lnk" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
takeown /f $path /r /d y 2>&1 | Out-Null
icacls $path /grant "${env:USERNAME}:F" /t 2>&1 | Out-Null
takeown /f $path 2>&1 | Out-Null
icacls $path /grant "${env:USERNAME}:F" 2>&1 | Out-Null
Remove-Item $path -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName $task.TaskName -TaskPath $task.TaskPath -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
reg.exe Load HKEY_USERS\Default "C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT" 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe delete "HKU\Default\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" /v "OneDriveSetup" /f 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe add "HKU\Default\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\OneDrive" /v "EnableTHDFFeatures" /t REG_DWORD /d "0" /f 2>&1 | Out-Null
Stop-Process -Name "regedit" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
reg.exe Unload HKEY_USERS\Default 2>&1 | Out-Null
reg.exe add $markerKey /v "DefaultUserConfigured" /t REG_SZ /d "$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')" /f 2>&1 | Out-Null
```

### 4.14 Advanced Tools – WIM utility / custom ISO
Extracts a Windows ISO, mounts `install.wim` (DISM), optionally injects drivers (driver categoriser separates storage/network/other drivers), converts ESD→WIM, generates an `autounattend.xml` that embeds the user's current Winhance configuration (registry tweaks, power settings, app-removal script) as first-logon/specialize scripts, and rebuilds a bootable ISO with `oscdimg` (the Windows ADK Deployment Tools are installed via winget when `oscdimg.exe` is missing). ESD↔WIM conversion uses `DISM /Export-Image /SourceImageFile:<src> /SourceIndex:<i> /DestinationImageFile:<dst> /Compress:<type> /CheckIntegrity`.

---

## 5. Sophia Script for Windows
**Type:** PowerShell module + preset file (`Sophia.ps1`), editions for Windows 10/11, LTSC, ARM and PowerShell 7. **Source:** https://github.com/farag2/Sophia-Script-for-Windows (MIT). **Launch:** `iwr script.sophia.team -useb | iex` downloads the right edition; then edit `Sophia.ps1` (uncomment/comment function calls) and run it, or call single functions (`.\Sophia.ps1 -Functions "DiagTrackService -Disable", "TaskbarAlignment -Left"`). Every tweak is a function with two (or more) parameter sets, one of which restores the Windows default. **Pre-flight (`InitialActions`)**: unblocks the script files, loads the localization, checks CPU architecture, PowerShell version and language mode, admin rights, ISE/VS Code, that the module is the latest version, that Windows is on the latest supported build, that Defender components exist and Defender is the active AV (and Controlled Folder Access off), pending reboots (CBS/Windows Update), BitLocker state, Secure Boot certificates, third-party entries in the `hosts` file, removed Microsoft Store/Feature Experience Pack, and it **refuses to run if traces of other tweakers are found** (e.g. `%SystemRoot%\AtlasModules` → AtlasOS, `Program Files (x86)\Revision Tool`, `HKLM\SOFTWARE\RemoveWindowsAI`, Ghost Toolbox, Win 10 Tweaker, BoosterX, Tron, defendnot …). **Post-run (`PostActions`)**: refreshes desktop/environment, restarts Start and Explorer (restoring open folders), opens Task Scheduler/Event Viewer if tasks or views were created, rebuilds the local GPO database from `LGPO.txt` (`LGPO.exe`), shows a toast and reports the size of restore points. A GUI front end (**Sophia Script Wrapper**, folder `Wrapper/`) drives the same functions. Data below: Windows 11 edition, module v7.3.0, every function from `Module/Sophia.psm1`; operations are the literal commands in each parameter-set branch. `Add-Policy`/`Remove-Policy` are Sophia helpers that record the policy in `%TEMP%\LGPO.txt`; at the end `LGPO.exe` rebuilds `%SystemRoot%\System32\GroupPolicy\Machine|User\Registry.pol` so the setting is also visible in gpedit.msc. “Preset default” = the call that is active (uncommented) in the shipped `Sophia.ps1`.

Total functions: **120**.

### Protection
#### Logging
Starts a transcript: `Start-Transcript -Path <script root>\Log-dd.MM.yyyy-HH-mm.txt -Force`.

#### CreateRestorePoint
Preset default: `CreateRestorePoint`

```powershell
# if System Protection is off for the system drive (checked via HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SPP\Clients):
Enable-ComputerRestore -Drive $env:SystemDrive

Checkpoint-Computer -Description "Sophia Script for Windows" -RestorePointType MODIFY_SETTINGS
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SystemRestore" -Name SystemRestorePointCreationFrequency -PropertyType DWord -Value 1440 -Force
```

### Privacy & Telemetry
#### DiagTrackService
**The Connected User Experiences and Telemetry (DiagTrack) service** · scope: Disabling the "Connected User Experiences and Telemetry" service (DiagTrack) can cause you not being able to get XBOX achievements anymore and affects Feedback Hub, Machine-wide

Preset default: `DiagTrackService -Disable`

Parameters: `-Disable` – Disable the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry (DiagTrack) service, and block connection for the Unified Telemetry Client Outbound Traffic; `-Enable` – Enable the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry (DiagTrack) service, and allow connection for the Unified Telemetry Client Outbound Traffic

`-Disable`:

```powershell
Get-Service -Name DiagTrack | Stop-Service -Force -PassThru
Get-Service -Name DiagTrack | Set-Service -StartupType Disabled -PassThru
Get-NetFirewallRule -Group DiagTrack -ErrorAction Ignore | Set-NetFirewallRule -Enabled True -Action Block
```

`-Enable`:

```powershell
Get-Service -Name DiagTrack | Set-Service -StartupType Automatic
Get-Service -Name DiagTrack | Start-Service
Get-NetFirewallRule -Group DiagTrack -ErrorAction Ignore | Set-NetFirewallRule -Enabled True -Action Allow
```

```powershell
New-Item -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Diagnostics\DiagTrack -Force
```

```powershell
New-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\DataCollection -Name MaxTelemetryAllowed -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Diagnostics\DiagTrack -Name ShowedToastAtLevel -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force
```

`-Default`:

#### ErrorReporting

```powershell
Get-Item -Path "$env:TEMP\LGPO.txt" -Force -ErrorAction Ignore | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting", "HKCU:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting" -Name Disabled -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
```

### OneDrive
#### OneDrive
**OneDrive** · scope: OneDrive user folder won't be removed if any file found there, Machine-wide

In preset but commented out (opt-in): `OneDrive -Uninstall`, `OneDrive -Install`, `OneDrive -Install -AllUsers`

Parameters: `-Uninstall` – Uninstall OneDrive; `-Install` – Install OneDrive depending on which installer is triggered

Common operations (all parameter sets):

```powershell
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\OneDrive -Name DisableFileSyncNGSC -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-Policy -Scope Computer -Path SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\OneDrive -Name DisableFileSyncNGSC
```

`-Uninstall`:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name OneDrive, OneDriveSetup, FileCoAuth -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Start-Process -FilePath $OneDriveSetup[0] -ArgumentList ($OneDriveSetup | Select-Object -Skip 1) -Wait
Remove-Item -Path $env:OneDrive -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Start-Process -FilePath "$env:SystemRoot\explorer.exe" -ArgumentList $env:OneDrive
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" -Name AutoRestartShell -PropertyType DWord -Value 0 -Force
Get-Process -Name explorer | Stop-Process -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" -Name AutoRestartShell -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force
Get-Process -Name UserOOBEBroker -ErrorAction Ignore | Stop-Process -Force
Start-Process -FilePath "$env:SystemRoot\System32\regsvr32.exe" -ArgumentList "/u /s $($_.FullName)" -Wait
Remove-Item -Path $OneDriveFolder -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction Ignore
Start-Process -FilePath "$env:SystemRoot\explorer.exe"
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Environment -Name OneDrive, OneDriveConsumer -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName *OneDrive* -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-Item -Path $Path -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
```

`-Install`:

```powershell
Start-Process -FilePath $env:SystemRoot\System32\OneDriveSetup.exe
$OneDriveURL = (Invoke-RestMethod @Parameters).root.update.amd64binary.url | Select-Object -Index 1
Invoke-WebRequest @Parameters
Start-Process -FilePath "$DownloadsFolder\OneDriveSetup.exe"
Get-Process -Name OneDriveSetup -ErrorAction Ignore | Stop-Process -Force
Remove-Item -Path "$DownloadsFolder\OneDriveSetup.exe" -Force
Remove-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\User Shell Folders" -Name "{B7BEDE81-DF94-4682-A7D8-57A52620B86F}" -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "OneDrive* Update*" -ErrorAction Ignore | Enable-ScheduledTask | Start-ScheduledTask
```

**Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)** · scope: The "Receive updates for other Microsoft products" setting will be enabled automatically to receive kernel updates, Machine-wide

In preset but commented out (opt-in): `Install-WSL `

Common operations (all parameter sets):

```powershell
$Distributions = Invoke-RestMethod @Parameters
Start-Process -FilePath $env:SystemRoot\System32\wsl.exe -ArgumentList "--install --distribution $($ButtonInstall.Tag)" -Wait
New-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings -Name AllowMUUpdateService -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force | Out-Null
```

### Gaming
#### XBOXGameBar

Preset default: `XBOXGameBar -Disable`

Parameters: `-Disable` – Disable XBOX Game Bar; `-Enable` – Enable XBOX Game Bar

`-Disable`:

```powershell
New-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\GameDVR -Name AppCaptureEnabled -PropertyType DWord -Value 0 -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\System\GameConfigStore -Name GameDVR_Enabled -PropertyType DWord -Value 0 -Force
```

`-Enable`:

```powershell
New-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\GameDVR -Name AppCaptureEnabled -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\System\GameConfigStore -Name GameDVR_Enabled -PropertyType DWord -Value 1 -Force
```

**XBOX Game Bar tips** · scope: Current user

Preset default: `XBOXGameTips -Disable`

Parameters: `-Disable` – Disable XBOX Game Bar tips; `-Enable` – Enable XBOX Game Bar tips

`-Disable`:

```powershell
New-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\GameBar -Name ShowStartupPanel -PropertyType DWord -Value 0 -Force
```

`-Enable`:

**Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling** · scope: Only with a dedicated GPU and WDDM version is 2.7 or higher. Restart needed, Machine-wide

`-Enable`:


`-Disable`:


### Scheduled tasks
#### CleanupTask
**The "Windows Cleanup" scheduled task for cleaning up Windows unused files and updates** · scope: A native interactive toast notification pops up every 30 days, Current user

Preset default: `CleanupTask -Register`

Parameters: `-Register` – Create "Windows Cleanup" scheduled task for cleaning up Windows unused files and updates; `-Delete` – Delete the "Windows Cleanup" and "Windows Cleanup Notification" scheduled tasks for cleaning up Windows unused files and updates

Built-in list `$VolumeCaches`: `BranchCache`, `Delivery Optimization Files`, `Device Driver Packages`, `Language Pack`, `Previous Installations`, `Setup Log Files`, `System error memory dump files`, `System error minidump files`, `Temporary Files`, `Temporary Setup Files`, `Update Cleanup`, `Upgrade Discarded Files`, `Windows Defender`, `Windows ESD installation files`, `Windows Upgrade Log Files`

Common operations (all parameter sets):

```powershell
Remove-Item -Path $Paths -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
```

`-Register`:

```powershell
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\PushNotifications -Name ToastEnabled -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Notifications\Settings\Windows.ActionCenter.SmartOptOut -Name Enable -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Notifications\Settings\Sophia -Name ShowBanner, ShowInActionCenter, Enabled -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\SystemSettings\AccountNotifications -Name EnableAccountNotifications -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer, HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer -Name DisableNotificationCenter -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\PushNotifications -Name NoToastApplicationNotification -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-Policy -Scope Computer -Path SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer -Name DisableNotificationCenter
Remove-Policy -Scope User -Path Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer -Name DisableNotificationCenter
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $_.PsPath -Name StateFlags1337 -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
New-Item -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\VolumeCaches\$VolumeCache" -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\VolumeCaches\$VolumeCache" -Name StateFlags1337 -PropertyType DWord -Value 2 -Force
New-Item -Path Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\AppUserModelId\Sophia -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\AppUserModelId\Sophia -Name DisplayName -Value Sophia -PropertyType String -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\AppUserModelId\Sophia -Name ShowInSettings -Value 0 -PropertyType DWord -Force
New-Item -Path Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\WindowsCleanup\shell\open\command -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\WindowsCleanup -Name "(default)" -PropertyType String -Value "URL:WindowsCleanup" -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\WindowsCleanup -Name "URL Protocol" -PropertyType String -Value "" -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\WindowsCleanup -Name EditFlags -PropertyType DWord -Value 2162688 -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\WindowsCleanup\shell\open\command -Name "(default)" -PropertyType String -Value 'powershell.exe -Command "& {Start-ScheduledTask -TaskPath ''\Sophia\'' -TaskName ''Windows Cleanup''}"' -Force
Get-Process -Name cleanmgr, Dism, DismHost | Stop-Process -Force
`$ProcessInfo.FileName = "`$env:SystemRoot\System32\cleanmgr.exe"
`$ProcessInfo.FileName = "`$env:SystemRoot\System32\Dism.exe"
New-Item -Path $env:SystemRoot\System32\Tasks\Sophia -ItemType Directory -Force
Set-Content -Path "$env:SystemRoot\System32\Tasks\Sophia\Windows_Cleanup.ps1" -Value $CleanupTaskPS -Encoding UTF8 -Force
$Action     = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute conhost.exe -Argument "--headless powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $env:SystemRoot\System32\Tasks\Sophia\Windows_Cleanup.ps1"
$Settings   = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -Compatibility Win8 -StartWhenAvailable
$Principal  = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId $SID -RunLevel Highest
Register-ScheduledTask @Parameters -Force
Set-Content -Path "$env:SystemRoot\System32\Tasks\Sophia\Windows_Cleanup_Notification.ps1" -Value $ToastNotificationPS -Encoding UTF8 -Force
(Get-Content -Path "$env:SystemRoot\System32\Tasks\Sophia\Windows_Cleanup_Notification.ps1" -Encoding UTF8).Replace('@""', '@"').Replace('""@', '"@') | Set-Content -Path "$env:SystemRoot\System32\Tasks\Sophia\Windows_Cleanup_Notification.ps1" -Encoding UTF8 -Force
$Action     = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute conhost.exe -Argument "--headless powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $env:SystemRoot\System32\Tasks\Sophia\Windows_Cleanup_Notification.ps1"
$Trigger    = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -DaysInterval 30 -At 9pm
```

`-Delete`:

```powershell
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskPath "\Sophia\" -TaskName "Windows Cleanup", "Windows Cleanup Notification" -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $_.PsPath -Name StateFlags1337 -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
Remove-Item -Path $Paths -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction Ignore
```

### Microsoft Defender & Security
#### NetworkProtection

Parameters: `-Enable` – Enable Microsoft Defender Exploit Guard network protection; `-Disable` – Disable Microsoft Defender Exploit Guard network protection


`-Disable`:


#### PUAppsDetection
**Detection for potentially unwanted applications** · scope: Machine-wide

Preset default: `PUAppsDetection -Enable`

Parameters: `-Enable` – Enable detection for potentially unwanted applications and block them; `-Disable` – Disable detection for potentially unwanted applications and block them

```powershell
Set-MpPreference -PUAProtection Enabled
```

`-Disable`:


`-Disable`:


```powershell
New-Item -Path HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging -Force

New-Item -Path "$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Event Viewer\Views" -ItemType Directory -Force
Set-Content -Path "$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Event Viewer\Views\ProcessCreation.xml" -Value $XML -Encoding UTF8 -NoNewline -Force
```

```powershell
Remove-Policy -Scope Computer -Path SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ModuleLogging -Name EnableModuleLogging
```

## 6. Sparkle (Parcoil)
**Type:** Electron + React desktop app (installer, also via winget/Scoop/Chocolatey). **Source:** https://github.com/Parcoil/Sparkle (GPL-3.0). Tweaks live in `tweaks/<id>/` with `meta.json` (title, risk, recommended, category, description) plus `apply.ps1` and optional `unapply.ps1`; the app runs them through elevated PowerShell (`executePowerShell`). Tweaks without `unapply.ps1` are not reversible. Other modules: Cleaner, DNS changer, App installer, Debloat/uninstaller, Restore points (Backup), system info dashboard with GPU detection (used to show NVIDIA-only tweaks).

### 6.1 Tweaks
43 tweaks.

#### Set 24-Hour Clock  
`24-hour-clock` · risk: safe · category: General, Appearance

> Switches Windows to a true 24-hour time format by updating the user’s regional time settings in the registry, affecting taskbar, apps, and system timestamps. IF HAVING ISSUES WITH TASKBAR, RESTART EXPLORER WITHIN SETTINGS

Apply:

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Control Panel\International" -Name "sShortTime" -Value "HH:mm"
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Control Panel\International" -Name "sTimeFormat" -Value "HH:mm:ss"
Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force
```

<details><summary>Unapply (revert)</summary>

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Control Panel\International" -Name "sShortTime" -Value "h:mm tt"
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Control Panel\International" -Name "sTimeFormat" -Value "h:mm:ss tt"
Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force
```

</details>

#### Debloat Windows  
`debloat-windows` · risk: safe · recommended · category: Performance, Privacy

> The user can choose between two methods to debloat Windows: 1. Sparkle Custom Selective Script: This method allows users to select which apps they want to keep. A WPF Window is presented where users can check or uncheck apps from a list. 2. Raphire's Win11Debloat Script: This method uses a well-known script that removes a wide range of built-in Windows apps and features. It is comprehensive and suitable for users who want a quick and effective way to debloat their system. Both remove bloatware and improve privacy by removing unnecessary Microsoft components, but they cater to different user preferences regarding control and convenience.

Apply (851 lines) – system-changing operations:

```powershell
Remove-AppxPackage -Package $_.PackageFullName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -PackageName $_.PackageName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
& ([scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod 'https://debloat.raphi.re/'))) -Silent -RemoveApps
```

_No unapply script – not reversible from the app._

#### Disable Background MS Store apps  
`disable-background-ms-store-apps` · risk: safe · category: Performance, Privacy

> Disables all background activity for modern UWP apps by setting 'GlobalUserDisabled' to 1 under the current user's BackgroundAccessApplications registry key, creating the key if it doesn't exist.

Apply:

```powershell
$path = "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\BackgroundAccessApplications"
$name = "GlobalUserDisabled"
$newValue = 1
  
# Ensure the key exists
If (-Not (Test-Path $path)) {
  New-Item -Path $path -Force | Out-Null
}
  
# Set the value
Set-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name $name -Type DWord -Value $newValue
  
Write-Host "$name set to $newValue (Background Access Disabled)"
```

<details><summary>Unapply (revert)</summary>

```powershell
$path = "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\BackgroundAccessApplications"
 $name = "GlobalUserDisabled"
 $originalValue = 0
 
 # Ensure the key exists
 If (-Not (Test-Path $path)) {
     New-Item -Path $path -Force | Out-Null
 }
 
 # Revert the value
 Set-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name $name -Type DWord -Value $originalValue
 
 Write-Host "$name reverted to $originalValue (Background Access Restored)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
```

</details>

#### Disable Telemetry  
`disable-telemetry` · risk: safe · recommended · category: Privacy, Performance

> Disables Windows telemetry by modifying registry keys to prevent data collection and reporting to ~~Microsoft~~ Microslop. This tweak was previously in sparkle but was removed issues with the tweak not applying correctly. It has been re-added.

Apply:

```powershell
# Registry tweaks
$registrySettings = @(
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AdvertisingInfo"; Name="Enabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Privacy"; Name="TailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticDataEnabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Speech_OneCore\Settings\OnlineSpeechPrivacy"; Name="HasAccepted"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Input\TIPC"; Name="Enabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization"; Name="RestrictImplicitInkCollection"; Value=1 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization"; Name="RestrictImplicitTextCollection"; Value=1 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization\TrainedDataStore"; Name="HarvestContacts"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Personalization\Settings"; Name="AcceptedPrivacyPolicy"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\DataCollection"; Name="AllowTelemetry"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced"; Name="Start_TrackProgs"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System"; Name="PublishUserActivities"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Siuf\Rules"; Name="NumberOfSIUFInPeriod"; Value=0 },

    # disable windows Error Reporting
    @{ Path="HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting"; Name="Disabled"; Value=1 },
    @{ Path="HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting"; Name="Disabled"; Value=1 },
    @{ Path="HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting"; Name="DontSendAdditionalData"; Value=1 },
    @{ Path="HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting"; Name="LoggingDisabled"; Value=1 },
    @{ Path="HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\Consent"; Name="DefaultConsent"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\Consent"; Name="DefaultOverrideBehavior"; Value=1 },

    # disable start menu tile suggestions and ads
    @{ Path="HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager"; Name="ContentDeliveryAllowed"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager"; Name="SubscribedContentEnabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager"; Name="OemPreInstalledAppsEnabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager"; Name="PreInstalledAppsEnabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager"; Name="PreInstalledAppsEverEnabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager"; Name="SilentInstalledAppsEnabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager"; Name="SystemPaneSuggestionsEnabled"; Value=0 },
    @{ Path="HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager"; Name="FeatureManagementEnabled"; Value=0 }
)

foreach ($reg in $registrySettings) {
    New-Item -Path $reg.Path -Force | Out-Null
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $reg.Path -Name $reg.Name -Value $reg.Value -Type DWord
}

# Disable Defender Auto Sample Submission
Set-MpPreference -SubmitSamplesConsent 2

# Disable Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service
Set-Service -Name diagtrack -StartupType Disabled

# Disable Windows Error Reporting Manager service
Set-Service -Name wermgr -StartupType Disabled

# Set SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB to total RAM in KB (this can help with performance)
$MemoryKB = (Get-CimInstance Win32_PhysicalMemory | Measure-Object Capacity -Sum).Sum / 1KB
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control" -Name "SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB" -Value [int]$MemoryKB

# Remove PeriodInNanoSeconds key if exists
Remove-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Siuf\Rules" -Name "PeriodInNanoSeconds" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

Write-Output "Telemetry settings have been applied. Bye Bye Microslop"
```

#### Enable HAGS  
`enable-hags` · risk: safe · category: Performance, Gaming, GPU

> Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS) is a Windows feature that shifts more GPU management and scheduling tasks from the CPU to the GPU, reducing CPU overhead and potentially improving performance and latency

Apply:

```powershell
$regPath = "HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\GraphicsDrivers"
$keyName = "HwSchMode"
$value = 2

If (-not (Test-Path $regPath)) {
    New-Item -Path $regPath -Force | Out-Null
}

Set-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name $keyName -Value $value -Type DWord

Write-Host "Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling enabled. A restart may be required."
```

#### Optimize Network Settings  
`optimize-network-settings` · risk: safe · category: Network, Gaming

> Applies a comprehensive set of netsh TCP/IP tweaks to disable latency-inducing features, enable fast open, offload networking tasks to hardware, fine-tune congestion control, and set optimal MTU, all to maximize speed, reduce CPU load, and improve responsiveness for gaming and high-performance internet use.

Apply:

```powershell
Write-Host "Applying network tweaks..."

netsh int tcp set heuristics disabled
netsh int tcp set supplemental template=internet congestionprovider=ctcp
netsh int tcp set global rss=enabled
netsh int tcp set global ecncapability=enabled
netsh int tcp set global timestamps=disabled
netsh int tcp set global fastopen=enabled
netsh int tcp set global fastopenfallback=enabled
netsh int tcp set supplemental template=custom icw=10

Write-Host "Network tweaks applied successfully."
```

<details><summary>Unapply (revert)</summary>

```powershell
netsh int tcp set global rss=default
netsh int tcp set global ecncapability=default
netsh int tcp set global timestamps=default
netsh int tcp set global fastopen=default
netsh int tcp set global fastopenfallback=default
netsh int tcp set supplemental template=custom icw=4

Write-Host "Network tweaks reverted to defaults."
```

#### Set PowerShell 7 as Default  
`set-powershell7-default` · risk: safe · category: General

> Sets PowerShell 7 as the default profile in Windows Terminal (installs PS7 if missing)

Apply:

```powershell
if (Test-Path -Path "$env:ProgramFiles\PowerShell\7") {
    Write-Host "PowerShell 7 is already installed."
} else {
    Write-Host "Installing PowerShell 7..."
    winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --silent
}

$targetTerminalName = "PowerShell"

if (-not (Get-Command "wt" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Write-Host "Windows Terminal not installed. Exiting..."
    exit
}

$settingsPath = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState\settings.json"
if (-not (Test-Path -Path $settingsPath)) {
    Write-Host "Windows Terminal settings.json not found."
    exit
}

$settingsContent = Get-Content -Path $settingsPath | ConvertFrom-Json
$ps7Profile = $settingsContent.profiles.list | Where-Object { $_.name -eq $targetTerminalName }

if ($ps7Profile) {
    $settingsContent.defaultProfile = $ps7Profile.guid
    $settingsContent | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 100 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath
    Write-Host "Default profile set to PowerShell 7"
} else {
    Write-Host "No PowerShell 7 profile found."
}
```

<details><summary>Unapply (revert)</summary>
