#### Ultimate Performance Power Plan  
`ultimate-performance-plan` · risk: caution · recommended · category: Performance, Gaming

> Enables the Ultimate Performance power plan by creating it if missing, retrieving its GUID, and activating it to maximize system responsiveness and performance by preventing power-saving limitations.

Apply:

```powershell
$ultimatePlan = powercfg -l | Select-String "Ultimate Performance"
  
  if (-not $ultimatePlan) {
      Write-Host "Ultimate Performance plan not found. Creating..." 
      powercfg -duplicatescheme e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61
  } else {
      Write-Host "Ultimate Performance plan already exists." 
  }
  
  # Get the GUID of the Ultimate Performance plan
  $ultimatePlanGUID = (powercfg -l | Select-String "Ultimate Performance").ToString().Split()[3]
  
  # Set it as the active plan
  powercfg -setactive $ultimatePlanGUID
  
  Write-Host "Ultimate Performance power plan is now active." 
```

<details><summary>Unapply (revert)</summary>

```powershell
$balancedGUID = "381b4222-f694-41f0-9685-ff5bb260df2e"
  
  # check if the Balanced plan exists
  $balancedExists = powercfg -l | Select-String $balancedGUID
  
  if ($balancedExists) {
      powercfg -setactive $balancedGUID
      Write-Host "Balanced power plan is now active." 
  } else {
      Write-Host "Balanced power plan not found. Creating a new Balanced plan..." 
      powercfg -duplicatescheme $balancedGUID
      powercfg -setactive $balancedGUID
      Write-Host "Balanced power plan created and activated." 
  }
```

#### Disable Windows Platform Binary Table  
`wpbt` · risk: caution · category: Privacy

> Windows Platform Binary Table (WPBT) allows manufacturers to execute software each boot, including drivers or anti-theft software. Disabling WPBT improves security by blocking this mechanism.

Apply:

```powershell
# Credit to Chris Titus Tech

$regPath = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager"
$regName = "DisableWpbtExecution"
$applyValue = 1

if (-not (Test-Path $regPath)) {
    New-Item -Path $regPath -Force | Out-Null
}

Set-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name $regName -Value $applyValue -Type DWord

Write-Host "WPBT execution disabled."
```

<details><summary>Unapply (revert)</summary>

```powershell
# Credit to Chris Titus Tech

$regPath = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager"
$regName = "DisableWpbtExecution"

if (Test-Path $regPath) {
    if (Get-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name $regName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        Remove-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name $regName
        Write-Host "WPBT execution restored to default."
    } else {
        Write-Host "Tweak was not applied."
    }
} else {
    Write-Host "Registry path does not exist, nothing to unapply."
}
```

</details>

| Recycle Bin | `Clear-RecycleBin -Force` |
| Windows Update cache | contents of `%SystemRoot%\SoftwareDistribution\Download` |

| Error reports | contents of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps` |

### 6.5 Debloat / uninstaller
Lists installed AppX packages and Win32 programs; removes AppX with `Remove-AppxPackage "<PackageFullName>"`, Win32 apps by running their `UninstallString` silently (`/S` for EXE installers, `msiexec /x {GUID} /quiet /norestart` for MSI).

### 6.6 Backup (restore points)
Creates restore points with `Checkpoint-Computer -Description '<name>'` after setting `HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SystemRestore\SystemRestorePointCreationFrequency = 0` (removes the 24 h cooldown); lists restore points (`Get-ComputerRestorePoint`), restores one (`Restore-Computer -RestorePoint <SequenceNumber>`) and can delete all restore points (`vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet`).

## 7. Winaero Tweaker
**Type:** closed-source freeware tweaker (Windows 7–11) by Sergey Tkachenko, current 1.65. **Site:** https://winaerotweaker.com. The UI is a categorised tree with search, bookmarks, “select visible tweaks”, per-tweak desktop shortcuts, **Import/Export** of all changes (`.ini`), and “Reset defaults” per page. Features not applicable to the running Windows build are hidden. Source code is not available; the right-hand column names the documented Windows setting each tweak manipulates (from Winaero’s own linked how-to articles / Microsoft documentation), so the exact write may differ slightly in implementation details.

| Category | Feature | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| Home | Information | Shows hardware/OS information (read-only). |
| Appearance | Aero Colors / Custom Accents / Colored Title Bars / Inactive Title Bars Color | Window frame, accent and title-bar colours via `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM` (`ColorPrevalence`, `AccentColor`, `AccentColorInactive`) and up to 8 custom accent colours shown in Settings > Colors. |
| Appearance | Aero Lite | Activates the hidden Aero Lite visual style (`aerolite.msstyles` theme). |
| Appearance | Alt+Tab Appearance | Transparency, desktop dimming, hide-windows, thumbnail size/spacing/margins of Alt+Tab (`HKCU\...\Explorer\MultitaskingView\AltTabViewHost` values such as `Grid_backgroundPercent`, `BackgroundDimmingLayer_percent`, `Wallpaper`); option for the classic icon-only Alt+Tab. |
| Appearance | Dark Color Scheme | App/system light-dark mode: `HKCU\...\Themes\Personalize` `AppsUseLightTheme` / `SystemUsesLightTheme`. |
| Appearance | Slow Down Animations | Enables slow-motion window animations while holding Shift (`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM` `AnimationsShiftKey = 1`). |
| Appearance | Startup Sound | Replace the boot sound with a custom .wav (disabled on Windows versions where the resource is protected). |
| Appearance | Theme Behavior | Stops themes from changing mouse pointers and desktop icons (`HKCU\...\Themes` `ThemeChangesMousePointers` / `ThemeChangesDesktopIcons = 0`). |
| Advanced Appearance | Icons, Menus, Message/Statusbar/System Font, Scrollbars, Window Borders, Window Title Bars, Reset | Classic window metrics under `HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\WindowMetrics` (e.g. `IconSpacing`, `IconVerticalSpacing`, `MenuHeight`, `ScrollWidth`, `ScrollHeight`, `BorderWidth`, `PaddedBorderWidth`, `CaptionHeight`, `CaptionFont`, `MenuFont`, `MessageFont`, `StatusFont`, `IconFont`); “Reset” restores defaults. Store/UWP apps ignore these metrics. Rewritten in 1.64.1. |
| Behavior | Chkdsk Timeout at Boot | Seconds before boot-time Chkdsk starts (`chkntfs /t:<sec>` → `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager` `AutoChkTimeout`). |
| Behavior | Disable Aero Shake | Stops shake-to-minimize (`HKCU\...\Explorer\Advanced` `DisallowShaking = 1`). |
| Behavior | Disable Aero Snap | Turns off window snapping (`HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop` `WindowArrangementActive = 0`). |
| Behavior | Disable App Lookup in Store | No “look for an app in the Store” for unknown file types (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer` `NoUseStoreOpenWith = 1`). |
| Behavior | Disable Automatic Maintenance | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\Maintenance` `MaintenanceDisabled = 1`. |
| Behavior | Disable Downloads Blocking | Stops the Zone.Identifier “downloaded from the internet” marking (`HKCU\...\Policies\Attachments` `SaveZoneInformation = 1`). |
| Behavior | Disable Driver Updates | No drivers via Windows Update (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate` `ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate = 1`). |

## 8. Autoruns (Sysinternals)
**Type:** Microsoft Sysinternals autostart viewer/manager, v14.3 (June 2026), GUI (`Autoruns.exe`/`Autoruns64.exe`) + CLI (`autorunsc.exe`). **Docs:** https://learn.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/autoruns. Not a tweaker: it lists every auto-start extensibility point (ASEP) and lets you disable or delete entries.

### 8.1 Tabs / scanned locations
| Tab | What is scanned (examples) |
|---|---|
| Logon | `HKLM\|HKCU\SOFTWARE\(WOW6432Node\)Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`, `RunOnce`, `RunOnceEx`, `Policies\Explorer\Run`, `...\Winlogon` `Userinit`/`Shell`, user and common Startup folders, Active Setup `Installed Components` |
| Explorer | Shell extensions, context-menu handlers, icon overlay handlers, `ShellServiceObjectDelayLoad`, `SharedTaskScheduler`, column handlers, copy hooks |
| Internet Explorer | Browser Helper Objects, toolbars, URL search hooks, extensions |
| Scheduled Tasks | All tasks in the Task Scheduler library |
| Services | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services` entries set to Automatic/Boot/System (non-disabled) |
| Drivers | Kernel drivers from the same Services key (Start 0–2) |
| Codecs | Media codecs, DirectShow filters, ACM/VfW drivers |
| Boot Execute | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager` `BootExecute`, `SetupExecute`, `Execute`, `S0InitialCommand` |
| Image Hijacks | `Image File Execution Options` `Debugger` values, `.exe`/`.cmd` file-association and command-processor `AutoRun` hijacks, `SilentProcessExit` monitors |
| AppInit | `...\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows` `AppInit_DLLs` (and WOW64) |
| KnownDLLs | `...\Session Manager\KnownDLLs` |
| Winlogon | Winlogon notification packages, GINA/credential providers |
| Winsock Providers | Winsock LSP/namespace providers |
| Print Monitors | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Monitors` |
| LSA Providers | `...\Control\Lsa` authentication/security/notification packages |
| Network Providers | `...\Control\NetworkProvider\Order` |
| WMI | WMI event consumers/filters/bindings (permanent subscriptions) |
| Sidebar Gadgets / Office | Gadgets (Vista/7) and Office add-ins |
| Everything | All of the above in one list |

### 8.2 Actions and options
- **Disable** (untick): the entry is kept but stops running. Registry-based entries are moved into an `AutorunsDisabled` subkey of the same key (Startup-folder items into an `AutorunsDisabled` subfolder); services/drivers get their Start value changed; scheduled tasks are disabled in Task Scheduler. Re-ticking restores them.
- **Delete** the entry, **Jump to Entry** (opens Regedit/Explorer/Task Scheduler at the location), **Jump to Image**, **Properties**, **Process Explorer** integration, **Search online**.
- **Options**: Hide empty locations, Hide Microsoft entries, Hide Windows entries, Hide VirusTotal-clean entries; **Scan options**: verify code signatures, check VirusTotal (hash lookup, optional upload of unknown files), scan only per-user locations.
- **User** menu: view autostarts of other user profiles; **Analyze offline system** (point at another Windows folder/hive); **Compare** with a saved `.arn` snapshot (highlights new entries); **Save/Export** as `.arn` or text/CSV.
- Colour coding: yellow = file not found, red/pink = unsigned or VirusTotal hits.

### 8.3 `autorunsc` (command line)
```text
autorunsc [-a <*|bdeghiklmoprsw>] [-c|-ct|-x] [-h] [-m] [-s] [-t] [-u] [-v[rs]] [-vt] [[-z <systemroot> <userprofile>] | [user|*]]
-a  selection: * all, b boot execute, d AppInit DLLs, e Explorer add-ons, g gadgets, h image hijacks,
    i IE add-ons, k KnownDLLs, l logon (default), m WMI, n Winsock/network providers, o codecs,
    p printer monitors, r LSA providers, s services + non-disabled drivers, t scheduled tasks, w Winlogon
-c CSV   -ct tab-delimited   -x XML   -h file hashes   -m hide Microsoft entries   -s verify signatures
-t normalized UTC timestamps   -u only unsigned / VirusTotal-unknown or flagged
-v[rs] VirusTotal lookup (r = open reports, s = upload unknown files)   -vt accept VirusTotal ToS
-z scan an offline Windows installation   user = account to show (* = all profiles)
```

## 9. Process Lasso (Bitsum)
**Type:** closed-source process automation/optimization (Free + Pro, lifetime licences), current v17. **Docs:** https://bitsum.com/apps/process-lasso/docs/. Architecture: GUI (`ProcessLasso.exe`) + core engine **Process Governor** (`ProcessGovernor.exe`, runs as user process or Windows service) that applies rules in real time; configuration in an INI file (also JSON), with config push/pull for enterprise deployment, command-line arguments and profile switching. It does not tweak the registry wholesale; it acts on running processes through Windows APIs, plus installs its own power plan. “Mechanism” below names the Windows facility used.

| Area | Feature | Edition | What it does / mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Algorithm | ProBalance | Free | Watches CPU use; when background processes hog the CPU it temporarily lowers their **priority class** (optionally affinity), then restores it. Foreground and excluded processes are left alone. Goal: responsiveness under load. Advanced settings: thresholds, durations, exclusions, restraint of child processes. |
| Algorithm | Performance Mode | Free | While designated processes (or auto-detected games) run, switches the active power plan (default **Bitsum Highest Performance**) and excludes the process from ProBalance; reverts afterwards. |
| Power | Bitsum Highest Performance power plan | Free | Custom power scheme installed by Process Lasso: no core parking, minimum processor state 100 %, maximum performance settings; tuned to prefer P-cores on hybrid CPUs (v14). |
| Power | IdleSaver | Free | Switches to an energy-saving power plan when the PC is idle, back when active. |
| Power | Application Power Profiles / Load-based Profile Switching / Config Profile Switcher | Pro (Power Plan Automation) | Activate a chosen power plan while specific apps run, or based on system load; switch whole configuration profiles. |
| Rule | CPU Priorities (persistent priority class) | Free | `SetPriorityClass` on every launch of the process. Since v15 **Registry Enforced Priorities**: writes the priority to `Image File Execution Options\<exe>\PerfOptions` (`CpuPriorityClass`, `IoPriority`) so Windows applies it even without Process Lasso running. |
| Rule | I/O priorities, Memory priorities, Thread priority boost | Free / Pro | Process I/O priority and memory (page) priority via `NtSetInformationProcess`; disable/enable dynamic priority boost. |
| Rule | CPU Affinities (persistent, named affinities v14) | Free | `SetProcessAffinityMask` applied on every launch; named affinity sets (e.g. “P-cores”, “CCD0”). |
| Rule | CPU Sets / System Reserved CPU Sets | Pro | Soft affinity via `SetProcessDefaultCpuSets`; reserve cores for specific processes system-wide. |
| Rule | Efficiency Mode (Windows 11) | Free | Persists Windows 11 Efficiency Mode (EcoQoS power throttling via `SetProcessInformation(ProcessPowerThrottling)` + low priority) on or off per process. |
| Rule | GPU priorities (v16) | Pro | Per-process GPU scheduling priority rules. |
| Rule | Foreground Boosting / Startup Boost | Pro | Raise priority of the foreground process, or of a process for a period after launch. |
| Rule | System Timer Resolution | Pro | Requests a higher global timer resolution (`NtSetTimerResolution`) while specified processes run. |
| Rule | Instance Count Limits | Pro | Limit how many instances of a process may run per session. |
| Rule | Keep Running | Pro | Restart a process automatically if it exits. |
| Rule | Auto-Terminate / Disallowed Processes | Pro | Terminate processes on start (block list). |
| Rule | Process Watchdog | Pro | Advanced triggers (CPU %, memory, duration) → actions (change priority/affinity, terminate, restart, power plan …). |
| Rule | Anti-Sleep Processes / Timed Keep PC Awake | Pro / Free | Prevent sleep while a process runs or for a set time (`SetThreadExecutionState`). |
| Algorithm | CPU Limiter | Pro | When a process exceeds X % CPU for Y s, temporarily reduces the number of cores it may use (affinity) for Z s. |
| Algorithm | Hard CPU Throttling | Pro | Hard cap of a process’ CPU usage. |
| Algorithm | Instance Balancer | Pro | Spreads multiple instances of the same app across different cores. |
| Algorithm | Processor Group Extender | Pro | Lets processor-group-unaware apps use all logical CPUs on systems with > 64 threads. |
| Algorithm | SmartTrim | Free | Periodically trims working sets of processes above a memory threshold and/or clears the standby list (file cache) when free memory is low. |
| System | Disable Hyper-Threading (SMT) option | Free | Option to stop using SMT sibling threads for processes. |
| UI | Graph, All/Active process tabs, Rules column flags, logging, keyboard shortcuts, rule import/export, consolidated rules view (v17) | Free | Responsiveness/CPU graph with ProBalance restraint markers; per-process CPU history; log viewer of every action. |

Companion apps: **ParkControl** (edit core parking & heterogeneous scheduling settings of power plans), CPU affinity calculator. Anti-cheat note: some anti-cheat systems block changing priority/affinity of protected game processes.

## 10. AtlasOS
**Type:** AME Wizard playbook (`.apbx`) that modifies an existing Windows 11 24H2/25H2 install (not a custom ISO); applied with **AME Wizard**. **Source:** https://github.com/Atlas-OS/Atlas (GPL-3.0), playbook v0.5.0. The playbook is a tree of YAML task files (`src/playbook/Configuration`); action types: `!registryValue`, `!registryKey`, `!service` (startup 0 Boot … 4 Disabled), `!scheduledTask`, `!appx`, `!file`, `!taskKill`, `!run`, `!cmd`, `!powerShell`, `!task` (include). “Condition `option …`” = only applied if that choice was ticked in AME Wizard. Requirements enforced by AME Wizard before running: Defender toggled off (temporarily), no 3rd-party AV, internet, no pending updates, UCPD (User Choice Protection Driver) disabled, plugged in. After install, the **Atlas folder** (`C:\Windows\AtlasDesktop`) contains toggle scripts to change/revert most choices (section 10.3), and the optional **AtlasOS Toolbox** app.

### 10.1 Install-time options (AME Wizard pages)
| Page | Options (default first) |
|---|---|
| Defender | **Enable Defender (recommended)** / Disable Defender |
| CPU security mitigations | **Default Windows mitigations** / Disable all mitigations |
| Automatic updates | **Disable automatic Windows Updates** / Enable automatic Windows Updates |
| Checkboxes | Disable Hibernation · Maximum Performance (disable power saving) · Disable Core Isolation |
| Checkboxes | Remove Snipping Tool app · Remove Microsoft Edge · Install a browser |
| Checkbox | Install Atlas Toolbox (beta) |
| Browser (if “install a browser”) | **Brave** / LibreWolf / Firefox / Chrome |

ISO mode (AME Wizard can also build a pre-configured ISO): disables BitLocker device encryption and hardware requirement checks.

### 10.2 Everything the playbook does (by task file)
##### Folder `.`

#### Root Playbook File  
`custom.yml`

> Runs all of the Playbook files

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SET | HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\PowerShell\1\ShellIds\Microsoft.PowerShell | ExecutionPolicy | REG_SZ | RemoteSigned |  |

- powerShell: `reg load HKU\AME_UserHive_Default C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT` (not in OOBE)

  ```powershell

  Remove-Item -LiteralPath "$windir\AtlasDesktop" -Force -Recurse
  Remove-Item -LiteralPath "$windir\AtlasModules" -Force -Recurse
  ```
  
  
- status: “Copying files”
- powerShell:

  ```powershell
  $windir = [Environment]::GetFolderPath('Windows')
  @(
      'AtlasModules',
      'AtlasDesktop'
  ) | ForEach-Object {
      if (!(Test-Path $_)) { exit 1 }
      Copy-Item -Path $_ -Destination $windir -Force -Recurse
      if (!$?) { exit 2 }
  }
  Start-Process -FilePath """$windir\AtlasDesktop\6. Advanced Configuration\Process Explorer\Uninstall Process Explorer.cmd""" -ArgumentList "/silent" -WindowStyle Hidden
  Copy-Item -Path 'Themes\*' -Destination """$windir\Resources\Themes""" -Force -Recurse
  ```

- run `explorer.exe `

- status: “Securing PowerShell execution policy”

<details><summary>Author comments in file</summary>

- some changes requires default user access. loading the hive before everything else is required
- Prevent annoying notifications during deployment
- Configure PowerShell first so that other PowerShell scripts work
- NGEN - .NET assemblies PowerShell optimization
- Disk Cleanup is run first so it can run in the background
- Set hidden Settings pages
- Done before everything else as scripts will overwrite it
- Main tasks
- Set hives to HKU default user
- Set all the correct paths if there are incorrect ones in the registry
- Unloading the hive
- Set PowerShell execution policy to RemoteSigned from the previous "Unrestricted"
- This allows Atlas folder scripts (local) to run while requiring signatures for downloaded scripts

</details>

Operations in referenced script `STOPFOLDERPROC.ps1`:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id $proc.Id -Force -ErrorAction Stop
& schtasks.exe /End /TN $candidate 1>$null 2>$null
Stop-ProcessesUnderRoots -RootsLower $rootsLower
```


Operations in referenced script `DISABLENOTIFS.cmd`:

```powershell
reg add "HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\userNotificationListener" /v "Value" /t REG_SZ /d "Deny" /f > nul
reg add "HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Notifications\Settings" /v "NOC_GLOBAL_SETTING_ALLOW_NOTIFICATION_SOUND" /t REG_DWORD /d "0" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\PushNotifications" /v "ToastEnabled" /t REG_DWORD /d "0" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\PushNotifications" /v "NoCloudApplicationNotification" /t REG_DWORD /d "1" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer" /v "DisableNotificationCenter" /t REG_DWORD /d "1" /f > nul
sc config WpnService start=disabled > nul
sc stop WpnService > nul 2>&1
sc stop "%%a" > nul
sc delete "%%a" > nul
```


Operations in referenced script `CLEANUP.ps1`:

```powershell
Get-Process -Name cleanmgr -EA 0 | Stop-Process -Force -EA 0
Set-ItemProperty -Path "$baseKey\$($entry.Key)" -Name 'StateFlags0064' -Value $entry.Value -Type DWORD
```

- >>> Description <<<
- Tweaks for disabling spying/tracking on Windows so
- that you have more privacy.

- related to impacting privacy, like advertising.
- privacy\apps

- privacy\cloud
- privacy\telemetry
- QOL
- >>> Description <<<
- QoL stands for Quality of Life, and are general
- modifications designed for making Windows easier and
- more pleasant to use for more advanced general users.
- QoL tweaks can be anything, but they are mostly to do
- with modifying the graphical user interface (GUI).
- qol\appearance
- qol\windows-update

<details><summary>Author comments in file</summary>

- The reason of removing those applications is that they might be sending user data,
- showing unwanted content and using hardware resources. They can also simply be annoyances
- that are never used. However, most of these applications can be reinstalled via
- Microsoft Store in case the user needs them.
- https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/application-management/apps-in-windows-10
- Get current AppX packages to deprovision removed ones afterward
- AppX Microsoft Teams
- Seems legacy - not in 23H2
- New AppX Teams in 24H2
- 24H2 Copilot app
- Other apps
- Removing using AME Wizard causes issues with Cross Device Experience Host installing
- - !appx: {name: 'Microsoft.YourPhone*', type: family}
- Prevent provisioned applications from being reinstalled
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/application-management/remove-provisioned-apps-during-update
- Clear caches of Client.CBS and more
- Start menu cache is cleared later

</details>

```powershell
New-Item "$srcPathExpanded\Manifests" -Force -ItemType Directory | Out-Null
New-Item -ItemType HardLink -Path "$srcPathExpanded\Manifests\$manifest" -Target $manifest.FullName | Out-Null
if (!(Test-Path $servicingPolicyKey)) { New-Item -Path $servicingPolicyKey -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $servicingPolicyKey -Name LocalSourcePath -Value "$srcPath" -Type ExpandString -Force
```

#### Initial Configuration  
`atlas/start.yml`

> Performs the preliminary configuration

- status: “Setting the environment”
- powerShell:

  ```powershell
  function Add-ToPath ([array]$Paths) {
        $machine = [System.EnvironmentVariableTarget]::Machine
        $separator = [IO.Path]::PathSeparator
  
        $Paths | ForEach-Object {
              if (!(Test-Path $_ -PathType Container)) {
                    Write-Error """Path '$_' doesn't exist as a container."""
              }
        }
  
        $newPath = @()
        $newPath += [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', $machine) -split $separator
        if ($newPath.Count -eq 0) { Write-Warning 'The PATH variable is currently empty.' }
        $newPath += $Paths
        $newPath = $newPath | Where-Object { $_ } | Select-Object -Unique
  
        [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', """$($newPath -join $separator)""", $machine)
  }
  
  $modulesPath = """$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Windows'))\AtlasModules"""
  Add-ToPath """$modulesPath""", """$modulesPath\Tools""", """$modulesPath\Scripts"""
  ```

`tweaks/misc/add-music-videos-to-home.yml`

> After disabling recent files in Quick Access, Music & Videos disappear. This fixes that.

- powerShell:

  ```powershell
  $o = new-object -com shell.application
  $currentPins = $o.Namespace('shell:::{679f85cb-0220-4080-b29b-5540cc05aab6}').Items() | ForEach-Object { $_.Path }
  foreach ($path in @(
      [Environment]::GetFolderPath('MyVideos'),
      [Environment]::GetFolderPath('MyMusic')
  )) {
      if ($currentPins -notcontains $path) {
          $o.Namespace($path).Self.InvokeVerb('pintohome')
      }
  }
  ```

#### Removes the drive letter from the EFI partition.  
`tweaks/misc/remove-efi-drive-letter.yml`

> This happens after clean install without formatting the drive

- powerShell:

  ```powershell
  try {
    # Find EFI System Partition on any disk
    $efiPartition = Get-Partition | Where-Object { $_.GptType -eq '{C12A7328-F81F-11D2-BA4B-00A0C93EC93B}' } | Select-Object -First 1
  
    if ($null -eq $efiPartition) {
      Write-Output "No EFI partition found, skipping."
      exit 0
    }
  
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($efiPartition.DriveLetter)) {
      Write-Output "EFI partition has no drive letter, skipping."
      exit 0
    }
  
    Write-Output "Removing drive letter '$($efiPartition.DriveLetter):' from EFI partition..."
    Remove-PartitionAccessPath -DiskNumber $efiPartition.DiskNumber -PartitionNumber $efiPartition.PartitionNumber -AccessPath "$($efiPartition.DriveLetter):\"
    Write-Output "Successfully removed EFI partition drive letter."
  }
  catch {
    Write-Output "Failed to remove EFI partition drive letter: $_"
    # Non-fatal error, continue installation
    exit 0
  }
  ```
  
  

<details><summary>Author comments in file</summary>

- Find EFI System Partition on any disk
- Non-fatal error, continue installation

</details>

#### Backup Atlas Services and Drivers  
`tweaks/scripts/script-backup2.yml`

> Backs up default Atlas services and drivers, after all the tweaks are finished

- powerShell: `.\BACKUP.ps1 -FilePath """$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Windows'))\AtlasModules\Other\atlasServices.reg"""`

#### Modify Client.CBS  
`tweaks/scripts/script-clientcbs.yml`

> Modifies components related to Client.CBS, the miscellaneous system package in Windows 10+

- powerShell: `.\CLIENTCBS.ps1`

Operations in referenced script `CLIENTCBS.ps1`:

```powershell
$viveZip = Get-ChildItem "ViVeTool-*.zip" -Name
$viveFolder = Join-Path -Path (Get-Location) -ChildPath "vivetool"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $viveFolder | Out-Null
Expand-Archive -Path $viveZip -DestinationPath $viveFolder -Force
throw "ViVeTool not found!"
if (!(Get-Command 'vivetool' -EA 0)) {
throw "ViVeTool EXE not found in ZIP!"
ViVeTool.exe /disable /id:$id | Out-Null
```


#### Disable Core Isolation  
`tweaks/scripts/script-core-isolation.yml`

> Disables Core Isolation (VBS) based on the user's options

- powerShell: `& """.\AtlasModules\Scripts\ScriptWrappers\ConfigVBS.ps1""" -DisableAllVBS`

Operations in referenced script `AtlasModules/Scripts/ScriptWrappers/ConfigVBS.ps1`:

```powershell
New-ItemProperty -Path $memIntegrity -Name "Enabled" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force # Need to be forced since Windows 11 24H2
New-ItemProperty -Path $kernelShadowStacks -Name "Enabled" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $kernelShadowStacks -Name "ChangedInBootCycle" -EA 0
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $kernelShadowStacks -Name "WasEnabledBy" -EA 0
New-ItemProperty -Path $credentialGuard -Name "Enabled" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $credentialGuard -Name "ChangedInBootCycle" -EA 0
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $credentialGuard -Name "WasEnabledBy" -EA 0
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" -Name "RunAsPPL" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard" -Name "EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $memIntegrity -Name "Enabled" -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $memIntegrity -Name "WasEnabledBy" -Value 2 -Type DWord
```

#### Set File Associations  
`tweaks/scripts/script-file-associations.yml`

> Sets file associations for the user-selected web browser and other apps

- run `FILEASSOC.cmd "Brave"` (option `browser-brave`)
- run `FILEASSOC.cmd "LibreWolf"` (option `browser-librewolf`)

#### Disable Service Host Splitting  
`tweaks/performance/system/disable-service-host-split.yml`

> Disables Service Host splitting for much lower RAM usage and process count, excluding XBOX services to fix issues with Game Bar

- powerShell:

  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services' |
    Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch 'Xbl|Xbox' } |
    Foreach-Object {
      if ($null -ne (Get-ItemProperty -Path """Registry::$_""" -EA 0).Start) {
        Set-ItemProperty -Path """Registry::$_""" -Name 'SvcHostSplitDisable' -Type DWORD -Value 1 -Force -EA 0
      }
    }
  ```
  
  

<details><summary>Author comments in file</summary>

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/application-management/svchost-service-refactoring

Operations in referenced script `TASKBARPINS.ps1`:

```powershell
$tmp = New-Item (Join-Path -Path $([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) -ChildPath $([System.Guid]::NewGuid())) -ItemType Directory -Force
Remove-Item -Path $taskBarAppData -Force
Get-ChildItem $taskBarAppData | Remove-Item -Force -Recurse
Copy-Item -Path "$tmp\*" -Destination $taskBarAppData -Force
reg add `"$key`" /v $($entry.Name) /t REG_BINARY /d `"$($entry.Value)`" /f | Out-Null
Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force
```

  ```powershell
  if ((Get-CimInstance -Class Win32_OperatingSystem).Caption -match 11) {$a = 'Windows 11'} else {$a = 'Windows 10'}; New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate' -Name 'ProductVersion' -Value $a -PropertyType String -Force
  ```

  ```powershell
  $ver = (Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion').DisplayVersion; New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate' -Name 'TargetReleaseVersion' -Value $ver -PropertyType String -Force
  ```

### 10.3 Atlas folder (post-install toggle scripts)
Every toggle first records its state in `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AtlasOS\Services\<Setting>` (`state`, `path`) so Atlas can re-apply it after upgrades, self-elevates, and then runs the operations listed. `%setSvc%` = `AtlasModules\Scripts\setSvc.cmd <service> <0-4>` which writes `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<service>\Start`.

#### .

**Install AtlasOS Toolbox**

```bat
powershell -EP Bypass -NoP ^& """$env:script""" %*
```


#### 1. Software

**Install Software**

```bat
powershell -EP Bypass -NoP ^& """$env:script""" %*
```


`InstallSoftware.ps1` operations:

```powershell
$Label.Text = "Download and install software using WinGet:"
& winget install -e --id $package --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements --disable-interactivity --force -h
```


**Install or Remove Edge**

```bat
powershell -EP Bypass -NoP ^& """$env:script""" %*
```


`RemoveEdge.ps1` operations:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://www.microsoft.com/robots.txt' -Method GET -TimeoutSec 10 -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
Remove-Item -Path $Path -Force -Recurse -Confirm:$false
Stop-Service -Name $service -Force
Stop-Process -Id $process -Force
$edgeUpdateApi = (Invoke-WebRequest 'https://edgeupdates.microsoft.com/api/products' -UseBasicParsing).Content | ConvertFrom-Json
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $link -Output $msi -UseBasicParsing
Start-Process -FilePath 'msiexec.exe' -ArgumentList "/i `"$msi`" /l `"$msiLog`" /quiet" -Wait
Start-Process -FilePath 'msiexec.exe' -ArgumentList "/fa `"$msi`" /l `"$msiLog`" /quiet" -Wait
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $link -Output $dlPath -UseBasicParsing
Start-Process -FilePath "$dlPath" -ArgumentList '/silent /install' -Wait
Start-Process cmd "/c PowerShell -NoP -EP Bypass -File `"$PSCommandPath`"" -Verb RunAs
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tempDirectory | Out-Null
Start-Process -FilePath "$tempDirectory\RemoveEdge.exe" -WindowStyle Hidden -Wait
```


**Remove Python Store Prompt**

```bat
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "Remove-Item -Path \"$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\WindowsApps\python*.exe\" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if (Test-Path Alias:python) { Remove-Item Alias:python }; if (Test-Path Alias:python3) { Remove-Item Alias:python3 }"
```

**Run Update Drivers**

```bat

```


`UpdateDrivers.ps1` operations:

```powershell

Install-Module -Name PSWindowsUpdate -Force -Scope CurrentUser -Confirm:$false
```


```powershell
if (!(Test-Path $powerKey)) { New-Item $powerKey | Out-Null }

```

#### 7. Security/Core Isolation (VBS)

**Current Configuration**

```bat

```


`ConfigVBS.ps1` operations:

```powershell
New-ItemProperty -Path $memIntegrity -Name "Enabled" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force # Need to be forced since Windows 11 24H2
New-ItemProperty -Path $kernelShadowStacks -Name "Enabled" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $kernelShadowStacks -Name "ChangedInBootCycle" -EA 0
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $kernelShadowStacks -Name "WasEnabledBy" -EA 0
New-ItemProperty -Path $credentialGuard -Name "Enabled" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $credentialGuard -Name "ChangedInBootCycle" -EA 0
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $credentialGuard -Name "WasEnabledBy" -EA 0
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" -Name "RunAsPPL" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard" -Name "EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity" -Value 0 -PropertyType DWORD -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $memIntegrity -Name "Enabled" -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $memIntegrity -Name "WasEnabledBy" -Value 2 -Type DWord
```


**Disable VBS**

```bat
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity" /t REG_DWORD /v Enabled /d "0" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard" /t REG_DWORD /v EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity /d "0" /f > nul
```


**Enable VBS**


#### 7. Security/Mitigations

**Disable All Mitigations**

```bat
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v "FeatureSettingsOverride" /t REG_DWORD /d "3" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v "FeatureSettingsOverrideMask" /t REG_DWORD /d "3" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "DisableExceptionChainValidation" /t REG_DWORD /d "1" /f > nul
PowerShell -NoP -C "Set-ProcessMitigation -System -Disable CFG" > nul
PowerShell -NoP -C "foreach ($a in $($env:enableCFGApps -split ' ')) {Set-ProcessMitigation -Name $a`.exe -Enable CFG}" > nul
bcdedit /set nx OptIn > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "MitigationAuditOptions" /t REG_BINARY /d "%mitigation_mask%" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "MitigationOptions" /t REG_BINARY /d "%mitigation_mask%" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager" /v "ProtectionMode" /t REG_DWORD /d "0" /f > nul
```


**Enable All Mitigations**

```bat
call RunAsTI.cmd "%~f0" "/main"
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v "FeatureSettingsOverrideMask" /t REG_DWORD /d "3" /f > nul
powershell -NonI -NoP -C "$proc = (Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object -First 1).Name; $env:CPU = if ($proc | sls 'Intel' -Quiet) {'0'} elseif ($proc | sls 'AMD' -Quiet) {'64'}"
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v "FeatureSettingsOverride" /t REG_DWORD /d "%CPU%" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "DisableExceptionChainValidation" /t REG_DWORD /d "0" /f > nul
PowerShell -NoP -C "Set-ProcessMitigation -System -Enable CFG"
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "MitigationAuditOptions" /t REG_BINARY /d "%mitigation_mask%" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "MitigationOptions" /t REG_BINARY /d "%mitigation_mask%" /f > nul
bcdedit /set nx AlwaysOn > nul
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager" /v "ProtectionMode" /t REG_DWORD /d "1" /f > nul
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Virtualization" /v "MinVmVersionForCpuBasedMitigations" /t REG_SZ /d "1.0" /f > nul
```


**Set Windows Default Mitigations**

```bat
reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v "FeatureSettingsOverride" /f > nul 2>&1
reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v "FeatureSettingsOverrideMask" /f > nul 2>&1
reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "DisableExceptionChainValidation" /f > nul 2>&1
reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "MitigationAuditOptions" /f > nul 2>&1
reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel" /v "MitigationOptions" /f > nul 2>&1
```

## 11. ReviOS
**Type:** AME Wizard playbook for Windows 10/11 (supported builds in `playbook.conf`: 19044, 19045, 22631, 26100, 26200, 26300, 28000), plus the companion **Revision Tool** app for post-install toggles. **Source:** https://github.com/meetrevision/playbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). Requirements enforced by AME Wizard: Defender toggled off, no pending updates, no third-party AV, internet. Same YAML action model as AtlasOS (see section 10). Install-time choice: default browser (**Brave** / Firefox / none). The playbook also writes OEM info/edition branding, imports a custom `hosts` file, sets the ReviOS wallpaper/theme, Start/taskbar layouts and file associations, and installs the Revision Tool.

- === Disable Wallpaper JPEG (.jpg) image Compression.
- === Disable system beeps.
- === Makes the Start Menu appear almost instantly when you click on the Windows icon in the Taskbar.
- === Specifies time (in milliseconds) that the mouse needs to remain over a window before the window is activated. (current setting is 10 ms)
- === Disables the blue screen that pops up when you're trying to shutdown or restart, asking you to save your work.
- === HungAppTimeout also specifies how long (5 seconds by default) the system waits for user processes to end after the user clicks/taps on the End task button in Task Manager.
- === The WaitToKillAppTimeout value determines how long the system waits for user processes to end after the user attempts to sign out, restart, or shut down Windows.
- === This value controls the timeout period in milliseconds for all low-level hooks.
- === Removes Ease of Access -> MouseKeys features tied to alteration of Sensitivity, so that it'll never change even when using MouseKeys.

- powerShell:

  ```powershell
  $folderTypesKey = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\FolderTypes'
  $downloadsFolderID = '{885a186e-a440-4ada-812b-db871b942259}'
  
  $path = Join-Path -Path $folderTypesKey -ChildPath $downloadsFolderID
  Get-ChildItem -Path $path -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
    if ((Get-ItemProperty -Path $_.PSPath).GroupBy) {
        Set-ItemProperty -Path $_.PSPath -Name GroupBy -Value ''
      }
  }
  ```
  
  
- powerShell:

  ```powershell
  $downloadsFolderID = '{885a186e-a440-4ada-812b-db871b942259}'
  $bagsPath = 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags'
  Get-ChildItem -Path $bagsPath | ForEach-Object {
    $fullPath = Join-Path -Path $_.PSPath -ChildPath 'Shell\{885A186E-A440-4ADA-812B-DB871B942259}'
    if (Test-Path -Path $fullPath) {
      Remove-Item -Path $fullPath -Recurse
    } 
  }
  ```

### Revision Tool (ReviOS companion app, `revitool.exe`)
**Source:** https://github.com/meetrevision/revision-tool (Flutter/Dart + Rust native helper). Installed by the ReviOS playbook into `%ProgramFiles%\Revision Tool`; every toggle is also a CLI command (`revitool tweaks <section> <toggle> enable|disable`, e.g. the playbook runs `revitool tweaks performance ntfs-last-access disable`, `... ntfs-8dot3-naming disable` and `... service-grouping set recommended`). Some writes run as TrustedInstaller. Toggles and the exact operations of their enable/disable methods:

#### performance
Data set `_userSvcSplitDisabled`: `CDPUserSvc_`, `OneSyncSvc_`, `WpnUserService_`

#### updates
##### `certificates`
run → `updateCertificates`:

```text
RUN PowerShell -NonInteractive -NoLogo -NoP -C "& {$tmp = (New-TemporaryFile).FullName; CertUtil -generateSSTFromWU -f $tmp; if ( (Get-Item $tmp | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).sum -gt 0 ) { $SST_File = Get-ChildItem -Path $tmp; $SST_File | Import-Certificate -CertStoreLocation "Cert:\LocalMachine\Root"; $SST_File | Import-Certificate -CertStoreLocation "Cert:\LocalMachine\AuthRoot" } Remove-Item -Path $tmp}
```

```text
SET HKLM\System\ControlSet001\Control\Session Manager\Power : HiberbootEnabled = 1,
SET HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System : HiberbootEnabled = 1,
# calls enableHibernation() first
```

disable:

```text
SET HKLM\System\ControlSet001\Control\Session Manager\Power : HiberbootEnabled = 0,
SET HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System : HiberbootEnabled = 0,
```

##### `modern-standby`
enable:

```text
DELETE VALUE HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power : PlatformAoAcOverride
```

disable:

```text
SET HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power : PlatformAoAcOverride = 0,
```

##### `tm-monitoring`
enable:

```text
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\GraphicsPerfSvc : Start = 2,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\Ndu : Start = 2,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\DPS : Start = 2,
```

disable:

```text
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\GraphicsPerfSvc : Start = 4,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\Ndu : Start = 4,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\DPS : Start = 4,
```

##### `usage-reporting`
enable:

```text
DELETE VALUE HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Session Manager\Power : SleepStudyDisabled
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\DPS : Start = 2,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\diagsvc : Start = 2,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\WdiServiceHost : Start = 2,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\WdiSystemHost : Start = 2,
```

disable:

```text
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Session Manager\Power : SleepStudyDisabled = 1,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\DPS : Start = 4,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\diagsvc : Start = 4,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\WdiServiceHost : Start = 4,
SET HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\WdiSystemHost : Start = 4,
```

## 12. Bulk Crap Uninstaller (BCUninstaller)
**Type:** free bulk program uninstaller (.NET 8, WinForms) with leftover/junk scanner, startup manager and built-in system tweaks. **Source:** https://github.com/Klocman/Bulk-Crap-Uninstaller (Apache-2.0); homepage https://www.bcuninstaller.com. Variants: Setup, Portable (self-contained runtime), `net` (needs .NET runtime). Requires admin rights. Data below: official manual (`doc/BCU_manual.html`) and source code (`UninstallTools/Factory`, `UninstallTools/Junk`, `ScriptHelper/Tweaks.cs`).

### 12.1 Application detection (where entries come from)
| Factory | Source |
|---|---|
| RegistryFactory | Uninstall keys `HKLM/HKCU\SOFTWARE\(WOW6432Node\)Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*` (normal installed programs, incl. MSI products, system components, updates) |
| StoreAppFactory | Microsoft Store / AppX apps (via `StoreAppHelper.exe /query`, removed with `StoreAppHelper /uninstall <FullName>`) |
| SteamFactory | Steam games (`SteamHelper.exe list/info/uninstall`) |
| ChocolateyFactory | Chocolatey packages (`choco list`, uninstall via `choco uninstall`) |
| ScoopFactory | Scoop packages |
| OculusFactory | Oculus apps (`OculusHelper.exe`) |
| WindowsFeatureFactory | Windows optional features (DISM), shown as uninstallable entries (“Uninstall Windows Features”) |
| WindowsUpdateFactory | Installed Windows updates |
| DirectoryFactory | Unregistered / orphaned programs found by scanning Program Files and other install folders (BCU generates a simple uninstaller if none exists) |
| PredefinedFactory | Built-in definitions for known apps (e.g. special handling for specific programs) |
| ScriptFactory | Custom XML “script” entries in `Resources\Scripts` (PowerShell uninstall + condition scripts) and the built-in system tweaks (12.6) |

Info adders that enrich every entry: `AppExecutablesSearcher`, `BasicIconGetter`, `CertificateGetter`, `ExecutableAttributeExtractor`, `FastSizeGenerator`, `FileIconGetter`, `GenerateSteamHelperStrings`, `KnownNameIconGetter`, `MsiInfoAdder`, `MsiUninstallStringGenerator`, `NsisQuietUninstallStringGenerator`, `PredefinedAppQuietUninstallStringGenerator`, `QuietUninstallStringCopier`, `SimpleDeleteUninstallStringGenerator`, `UninstallerSearcher`, `UninstallerTypeAdder`, `VersionCleaner`, `WebBrowserMarker` – e.g. reading MSI data, generating **quiet uninstall strings** for Inno Setup (`"<unins000.exe>" /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART`), MSI (`MsiExec.exe /qb /X{GUID} REBOOT=ReallySuppress /norestart`) and NSIS (wrapped in `UninstallerAutomatizer.exe Nsis [/K] <UninstallString>`, which clicks through the NSIS wizard automatically), verifying uninstaller certificates, computing sizes, detecting 64-bit, install date/location, icons, and marking web browsers. Chocolatey packages are listed with `choco list -lo -nocolor --detail` and removed with `choco uninstall <name> -y -r` (+ `-n --skipautouninstaller` for the quiet/forced variant).

### 12.2 Main functions
- **Uninstall / Uninstall quietly**: runs the selected uninstallers in bulk; quiet mode uses silent switches/UI automation so no clicks are needed (loud uninstallers can be dropped from a quiet task). Intelligent sorting runs loud uninstallers first.
- **Concurrent uninstallation** (experimental): runs several uninstallers at once with collision checks.
- **Uninstall using MsiExec**: uses the product GUID (`msiexec /x {GUID}`) when the normal uninstaller is broken.
- **Uninstall manually**: skips the uninstaller and lists files + registry keys to delete by hand.
- **Clean up “Program Files” folders**: finds empty folders and leftovers of partially uninstalled apps in default install locations.
- **Find by window**: drag a crosshair onto a window to find the owning application.
- **Uninstall Windows Features**, Store apps, Steam games, updates – all handled as normal list entries.
- **Startup Manager** (`BCUninstaller /sm`): view/disable/delete autostart entries from `HKLM`/`HKCU ...\CurrentVersion\Run` and `RunOnce` (incl. WOW6432Node), the user and common Startup folders, scheduled tasks, services and browser helper objects; entries can be disabled the same way Task Manager does it (binary flag in `HKLM|HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\StartupApproved\Run|Run32|RunOnce|StartupFolder`; older Windows: entries moved to a backup location) and re-enabled later, deleted, or opened in Explorer/Regedit; startup entries belonging to an app are also offered as junk after uninstall.
- **Before uninstalling**: optional System Restore point, process-kill window for programs that lock files.
- **During**: progress window with Run now / Skip / Terminate per uninstaller, “Prevent shutdown/restart” of uninstallers.
- **After**: **leftover/junk scan** with confidence ratings (12.3); registry entries are backed up as `.reg` before removal, files go to the Recycle Bin.
- **Application list extras**: highlight colours (orphaned, missing uninstaller, protected, Store app, system component, update), certificate verification, community user rating (synced to statistics server), treemap of disk usage, advanced filtering/uninstall lists (`.bcul`), advanced copy to clipboard, export to XML, “Simulate uninstallation” test mode, “Disable protection”.

### 12.3 Leftover (junk) scanners
After uninstalling, these scanners search for remnants; each finding gets a confidence level (VeryGood, Good, Questionable, Bad, Unknown). Only Good or better is pre-selected.

### 12.4 Advanced filtering / uninstall lists (`.bcul`)
Filters (include/exclude) with conditions on any property (DisplayName, Publisher, InstallLocation, …) using Contains, Contains any, Equals, Starts/Ends with, Regex (optionally negated). Saved as `.bcul` and usable for unattended removal.

### 12.5 Command line
```text
BCUninstaller.exe [path\list.bcul]          # open with an uninstall list
BCUninstaller.exe /sm                         # start only the Startup Manager
BCU-console uninstall <list.bcul> [/Q] [/U] [/V] [/J=<Level>]
   /Q quiet uninstallers where possible, /U unattended (no confirmation), /V verbose,
   /J=<VeryGood|Good|Questionable|Bad|Unknown> remove leftover junk after uninstall (default VeryGood)
BCU-console export out.xml                    # export installed application data
StoreAppHelper /query | /uninstall <FullName>
SteamHelper u[ninstall] [/s] <AppID> | i[nfo] <AppID> | l[ist] | steam
OculusHelper /query | /uninstall <CanonicalName>
UninstallerAutomatizer Nsis [/K] <UninstallCommand>   # automates clicking through NSIS uninstallers
```

## 13. NVCleanstall (TechPowerUp)
**Type:** closed-source NVIDIA driver customizer, current 1.19.0 (`winget install TechPowerUp.NVCleanstall`). Builds a custom GeForce driver package containing only the components you pick, then runs NVIDIA’s installer (`setup.exe`) on it or saves the package.

### 13.1 Workflow
1. **Driver source**: install best driver for the detected GPU, pick any version (incl. Studio/older), or **use driver files on disk** (e.g. hotfix drivers).
2. **Components**: tick/untick every package in the driver (display driver, PhysX, HD Audio, USB-C/VirtualLink, 3D Vision/stereo, Shield/Streaming, telemetry, FrameView SDK, NVIDIA App/GeForce Experience parts, notebook optimization, Ansel, etc.). Dependencies are resolved automatically.
3. **Tweaks** page (below).
4. **Install** directly or **build package** to a folder (a `-y` argument to the built setup gives an unattended install); optional automatic acceptance of the “driver unsigned” warning when the package was modified.

### 13.2 Tweaks
| Tweak | What it does |
|---|---|
| Disable Installer Telemetry & Advertising | Removes NVIDIA installer telemetry/ads and the telemetry component (NvTelemetry) from the package. |
| Unattended Express Installation | Runs the NVIDIA setup silently with default options; optional “disable automatic reboot”. |
| Perform a Clean Installation | Pre-checks NVIDIA’s own “clean install” (resets driver profiles/settings). |
| Enable Message Signaled-Based Interrupts (MSI mode) | Sets the GPU to MSI interrupt mode: `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\PCI\<GPU>\<instance>\Device Parameters\Interrupt Management\MessageSignaledInterruptProperties` `MSISupported = 1` (applied through the driver package; modified packages may need the signature rebuild below). |
| Disable Multiplane Overlay (MPO) | Turns off DWM multi-plane overlays (added 1.15; fixes rare stutter/flicker). The standard Windows switch for this is `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Dwm` `OverlayTestMode = 5`. |
| Remove NVENC concurrent session limit | Patches the driver with keylase/nvidia-patch so more than the default number of parallel NVENC encode sessions are allowed (added 1.15; “experimental” label removed in 1.17). |
| Disable NVIDIA HD Audio device sleep timer | Keeps the GPU HDMI/DP audio device awake (fixes cut-off audio, e.g. VR headsets) – added 1.1.0. |
| Disable HDCP | Disables HDCP in the driver configuration (e.g. for capture devices). |
| Add support for unsupported GPUs / modify INF | Edits the package INF (e.g. hardware IDs) – requires driver signature rebuild. |
| Rebuild digital signature | Re-signs a modified package with a locally generated certificate so Windows accepts it (24H2 fix in 1.17). |

Other: shows whether the installed driver is a Studio driver, links to the driver changelog, background check for new drivers, low-resolution friendly UI. (Exact tweak names can vary slightly between versions; NVCleanstall is closed source – details from TechPowerUp release notes.)

---

## 14. Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU, Wagnardsoft)
**Type:** closed-source driver removal tool for NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPU drivers (newer versions also handle selected audio drivers such as Realtek and Sound Blaster). **Site:** https://www.wagnardsoft.com. Recommended use: when a normal uninstall fails or when switching GPU brand; ideally run in **Safe Mode** with the network disconnected.

### 14.1 What a clean does
- Stops and removes the vendor services and drivers (e.g. `nvlddmkm`, NVIDIA Display Container `NVDisplay.ContainerLocalSystem`, AMD `amdkmdag`/`AMD External Events Utility`, Intel `igfx*`), removes the GPU device instances and **deletes the driver packages from the Driver Store** (`C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\nv*.inf_*`, `u0*`/`c0*` for AMD, `iigd*` for Intel) so Windows cannot reinstall them silently.
- Deletes vendor folders and caches: `C:\Program Files\NVIDIA Corporation`, `C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA*`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\DXCache/GLCache`, AMD `C:\AMD`, `C:\Program Files\AMD`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AMD`, Intel graphics folders, shader caches.
- Deletes vendor registry keys: software keys (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\NVIDIA Corporation`, `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AMD`, `ATI Technologies`, Intel GFX keys), service keys, display class keys (`{4d36e968-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}\00xx`), uninstall entries, COM/shell extensions, scheduled tasks and Run entries of the vendor software.
- Optional removal of: PhysX, GeForce Experience / NVIDIA App, NVIDIA Broadcast, Vulkan runtime registrations, AMD audio bus / AMD KMPFD (`-removeamdkmpfd`), monitors (display device entries, `-removemonitors`), C:\AMD / C:\NVIDIA installer folders.

### 14.2 Actions
- **Clean and restart** (recommended), **Clean and do NOT restart**, **Clean and shutdown** (for physically swapping the GPU). Device type selector (GPU / Audio) and vendor selector.
- **Safe-mode helper**: offers to reboot into Safe Mode (`bcdedit /set {current} safeboot minimal`, reverted after the clean).
- **Prevent downloads of drivers from Windows Update** when Windows searches for a device driver: sets the Device Installation setting `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\DriverSearching` `SearchOrderConfig = 0`; a button restores the default.
- Create a **System Restore point**, logging (saved to the DDU folder), check for updates, language selection.

### 14.3 Command line (from the developer)
```text
"Display Driver Uninstaller.exe" [options]
-silent                  run without UI
-restart                 reboot after cleaning
-cleannvidia | -cleanamd | -cleanintel     vendor to clean
-preventwinupdate        block driver downloads from Windows Update
-removemonitors          also remove monitor devices
-removeamdaudiobus  -removeamdkmpfd        extra AMD components
-removegfe               also remove GeForce Experience
-createsystemrestorepoint  -logging  -nosafemodemsg
example: "Display Driver Uninstaller.exe" -silent -restart -cleannvidia -preventwinupdate
```

---

## 15. RemoveWindowsAI (zoicware)
**Type:** single PowerShell script (Windows PowerShell 5.1 only) with WPF UI and CLI. **Source:** https://github.com/zoicware/RemoveWindowsAI. **Launch:** `& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zoicware/RemoveWindowsAI/main/RemoveWindowsAi.ps1")))`; CLI: `-nonInteractive -AllOptions`, `-nonInteractive -Options DisableRegKeys,RemoveAppxPackages,…`, `-ExcludeOptions`, `-InstallClassicApps photoviewer,mspaint,snippingtool,notepad,photoslegacy`, `-backupMode` (creates a restore point and backups so everything can be reverted), `-revertMode` (re-enables everything), `-RunWinUpdateRepair`, `-EnableLogging`. Many steps run as **TrustedInstaller/SYSTEM** (`Run-Trusted` creates a temporary scheduled task running as SYSTEM that starts the TrustedInstaller service and executes the command with its token). Policies are written both to the registry and into the local GPO `Registry.pol` (`Edit-PolFile`) so they look like gpedit changes. Feature flags are switched with `Set-FeatureID` (ViVeTool-style: `Reg.exe add HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\<obfuscated ID> /v EnabledState /t REG_DWORD /d 1` (1 = disabled, 2 = enabled)). The update-cleanup feature records the OS build under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\RemoveWindowsAI` (the key Sophia Script looks for). In the operations below, `@('a','b')[$revert]` means: value `a` when removing, value `b` when reverting.

| CLI option | Function | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `DisableRegKeys` | `Disable-Registry-Keys` | Disable registry keys/policies for Copilot, Recall, Click to Do, Input Insights, Copilot in Edge, Paint/Notepad/Photos AI, AI Fabric service, AI Actions, Voice Access, voice effects, AI in Settings search, Gaming Copilot, Office Copilot |
| `PreventAIPackageReinstall` | `Install-NOAIPackage` | Install a custom CBS (servicing) package so Windows Update does not reinstall the AI packages |
| `DisableCopilotPolicies` | `Disable-Copilot-Policies` | Edit IntegratedServicesRegionPolicySet.json to switch off Copilot/Recall region policies |
| `RemoveAppxPackages` | `Remove-AI-Appx-Packages` | Remove all AI AppX packages incl. “NonRemovable” ones and WindowsWorkload packages |
| `RemoveRecallFeature` | `Remove-Recall-Optional-Feature` | Remove the Recall optional feature |
| `RemoveCBSPackages` | `Remove-AI-CBS-Packages` | Remove hidden/locked AI packages from the CBS store |
| `RemoveAIFiles` | `Remove-AI-Files` | Delete remaining AI installers, files, registry keys and package folders |
| `HideAIComponents` | `Hide-AI-Components` | Hide the Settings page “AI Components” |
| `DisableRewrite` | `Disable-Notepad-Rewrite` | Disable Rewrite (AI) in Notepad |
| `RemoveWindowsAITasks` | `Remove-WindowsAI-Tasks` | Forcibly remove all Windows AI scheduled tasks |
| `UpdateCleanupCheck` | `Update-Cleanup-Check` | Create a scheduled task that re-runs the removal after Windows updates |
| `DisableDefenderAI` | `Disable-DefenderAI` | Disable the Defender AI platform host process/settings |

`Set-FeatureID` implementation:

```powershell
param(
    [switch]$enable,
    [switch]$disable,
    [uint32]$FeatureId
)

$regID = ObfuscateFeatureId $FeatureId
# 1 = disabled 2 = enabled
$value = @('1', '2')[[int]([bool]$enable)]
Reg.exe add "HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\$regID" /v 'EnabledState' /t REG_DWORD /d "$value" /f 
```

### `UpdateCleanupCheck` → `Update-Cleanup-Check`
> Create a scheduled task that re-runs the removal after Windows updates

```powershell
Reg.exe add 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\RemoveWindowsAI' /v $regValName /d "$OSBuild" /t REG_SZ /f >$null
$scriptContent = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zoicware/RemoveWindowsAI/refs/heads/main/RemoveAI-UpdateCleanup.ps1' -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object Content
Set-Content -Path $scriptPath -Value $scriptContent.Content -Force
$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'conhost.exe' -Argument "--headless powershell.exe -ep bypass -f `"$scriptPath`""
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogOn
$principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId 'S-1-5-18'
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskPath '\' -TaskName 'RemoveAI-UpdateCleanupChecker' -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Principal $principal -Settings $settings -Force | Out-Null
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'RemoveAI-UpdateCleanupChecker' -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item "$env:ProgramData\RemoveAI-UpdateCleanup-Silent.vbs" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -Force
```

- `Create-RestorePoint` (backup mode), `Check-PendingUpdates` (refuses to run with pending updates), `Update-Repair` / `-RunWinUpdateRepair` (stops BITS/wuauserv/DoSvc/UsoSvc/WaaSMedicSvc, kills `TiWorker.exe`, deletes `SoftwareDistribution`, `catroot2`, WU logs and reboot-pending keys, renames `WinSxS\pending.xml`), desktop shortcut creation, logging. `OtherAIFeatures.md` lists AI settings that must be disabled manually (e.g. in Edge, Office and app settings).

---

## 16. CrapFixer (Builtbybel)
**Type:** small WinForms (.NET) tool in classic “Analyze → Fix” style. **Source:** https://github.com/builtbybel/CrapFixer (MIT). **Analyze** reads every value of the tweak database and colours items red (not yet fixed) or grey (already in the recommended state); **Run Fixer** writes the `RecommendedValue`s; **Restore/Undo** writes the `DefaultValue` (`<deletevalue>` = delete the value, `<delete>` = delete the key). All tweaks are data-driven from `Wintweak2.ini` (registry tweaks) and `Winappx.ini` (bloat apps); both databases can be updated online from the GitHub repo (`DatabaseUpdateService`). Extra features: **App remover** (removes selected AppX packages with `Remove-AppxPackage -Package <full name>`), **Custom tweaks** (your own `.ini` tweak files in `%APPDATA%\CrapFixer\CustomTweaks`, same format), **Extensions** (downloadable PowerShell scripts from an online catalogue), **F1 / Help** online lookup, an optional **AI explainer** that sends a tweak definition to an AI model for a plain-language explanation, and an online **log analyzer** website for the fix log.

## 17. Flyoobe (Builtbybel, successor of Flyby11)
**Type:** Windows setup companion (WinForms/.NET, native controls): Windows 11 upgrade on unsupported hardware + OOBE/post-install configuration (rules, apps, debloat, personalization, accounts). **Source:** https://github.com/builtbybel/Flyoobe (MIT). **Version note:** Flyoobe 3 (3.0x) is current. The repository's `Flyoobe/` project is named `Flyoobe3.csproj` and is what is documented here, while the README states that the cleaned-up, refactored 3.x source is still being prepared for publication. Flyoobe 2.4 and Flyby11 Classic are legacy downloads.

### 17.1 Main features
- **Overview / recommendations**: checks the PC against transparent, file-based rules (`Flyoobe.ini` + optional `Flyoobe2.ini`, same format as CrapFixer: registry key/value, recommended vs default value); matching items stay collapsed, items needing attention are shown; apply or revert per rule.
- **Accounts**: opens `ms-settings:emailandaccounts` / `ms-settings:otherusers`, and the Windows local-account wizard via `explorer.exe ms-cxh:localonly` (Windows itself handles the account creation).
- **Network / Windows Update / About**: shortcuts to `ms-settings:network-status`, `ms-settings:windowsupdate-action`, `ms-settings:about`.
- **Browser / apps**: detects installed browsers, installs checked apps from `Apps.ini` with `winget.exe install` (one call per ID), and opens `ms-settings:defaultapps` to set the default.
- **Bloatware**: review and remove preinstalled AppX packages only after confirmation (`Bloatware.ini`, `Remove-AppxPackage -Package '<full name>'`).
- **Personalization**: writes `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize` `AppsUseLightTheme` / `SystemUsesLightTheme` (0 = dark) and `EnableTransparency`, and `HKCU\...\Explorer\Advanced\TaskbarAl` (0 = left), then broadcasts the settings change / restarts Explorer.
- **Recipes**: export/import a repeatable setup “recipe” (selected rules, apps, removals, personalization) as plain data, no embedded code; a review mode shows what a recipe would change.
- **Setup Actions** (optional, disabled by default in Settings > Advanced): local PowerShell packages in `Data\Actions\<id>\action.ini` + `run.ps1` with live output; recipe-safe actions can run in `Prepare`/`Finish` phases (see 17.5).
- **AI explainer** (optional): explains a rule in plain language.
- **Upgrade (Flyby11 heritage)**: in-place upgrade to Windows 11 on hardware that fails the checks. Pre-checks from `Upgrade.ini` (below). The ISO is mounted (`Mount-DiskImage`); in Flyby mode setup is started as `sources\setupprep.exe /Product Server` (the Windows Server setup path skips the TPM 2.0 / CPU / Secure Boot checks), otherwise the normal `setup.exe`. The legacy Flyby11 also offered `reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\Setup\MoSetup /v AllowUpgradesWithUnsupportedTPMOrCPU /t REG_DWORD /d 1` and ISO download via the Fido script.

`Upgrade.ini` checks: [Windows11] MinimumRamGB=4, RecommendedFreeSpaceGB=25, MinimumMediaBuild=22000, Require64Bit=true, RequireTpm20=true, RequireSecureBoot=true

### 17.5 Setup Actions (optional asset)
#### Chris Titus Tech's Windows Utility  
`christitus-winutil` · admin

> Downloads and starts the current WinUtil script from its official project endpoint.

```powershell
$source = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop
```

#### Clear the Windows icon cache  
`clear-icon-cache`

> Rebuilds the current user's icon cache after setup. Explorer is restarted once.

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\IconCache.db" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Start-Process explorer.exe
Start-Process explorer.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

#### Create a restore point  
`create-restore-point` · admin

> Creates a Windows system restore point before the remaining recipe changes are applied.

```powershell
Enable-ComputerRestore -Drive "$env:SystemDrive\"
Checkpoint-Computer -Description 'Before Flyoobe setup' -RestorePointType 'MODIFY_SETTINGS'
```

#### Default power plan  
`default-power-plan`

> Choose one of the built-in Windows power plans.

```powershell
powercfg -setactive SCHEME_MIN
powercfg -setactive SCHEME_BALANCED
powercfg -setactive SCHEME_MAX
```

#### Microsoft Defender maintenance  
`defender-maintenance`

> Update, repair or inspect Microsoft Defender using the original dynamic Flyoobe script.

```powershell
# Microsoft Defender maintenance (update signatures, repair, show status)
# Options: Update signatures; Repair definitions and update; Show Defender status

param([string]$choice)

function Get-MpCmdPath {
    $candidates = @(
        "$env:ProgramFiles\Windows Defender\MpCmdRun.exe",
        "$env:ProgramFiles\Microsoft Defender\MpCmdRun.exe"
    )
    foreach ($p in $candidates) { if (Test-Path $p) { return $p } }
    return $null
}

function Is-Admin {
    $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
    $pr = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($id)
    return $pr.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
}

function Show-Status {
    try {
        $s = Get-MpComputerStatus
        Write-Output "=== Microsoft Defender Status ==="
        Write-Output ("Engine version:           {0}" -f $s.AMEngineVersion)
        Write-Output ("Platform version:         {0}" -f $s.AMProductVersion)
        Write-Output ("AV signature version:     {0}" -f $s.AntivirusSignatureVersion)
        Write-Output ("AV signature last update: {0}" -f $s.AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated)
        Write-Output ("AS signature version:     {0}" -f $s.AntispywareSignatureVersion)
        Write-Output ("Real-time protection:     {0}" -f $s.RealTimeProtectionEnabled)
        Write-Output ("NIS enabled:              {0}" -f $s.NISEnabled)
        Write-Output ("Service enabled:          {0}" -f $s.AMServiceEnabled)
    } catch {
        Write-Output "✘ Failed to read Defender status: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}

switch ($choice) {

    "Update signatures" {
        if (-not (Is-Admin)) {
            Write-Output "ℹ Tip: Run as Administrator for the most reliable results."
        }

        try {
            # Primary: PowerShell cmdlet
            Update-MpSignature -ErrorAction Stop
            Write-Output "✔ Signatures updated via Update-MpSignature."
        } catch {
            # Fallback: MpCmdRun
            $mp = Get-MpCmdPath
            if ($mp) {
                Write-Output "↻ Falling back to MpCmdRun.exe ..."
                & $mp -SignatureUpdate | Out-String | Write-Output
            } else {
                Write-Output "✘ MpCmdRun.exe not found and Update-MpSignature failed."
            }
        }

        Show-Status
    }

    "Repair definitions and update" {
        if (-not (Is-Admin)) {
            Write-Output "✘ Please run this action as Administrator (required to reset definitions)."
            break
        }

        $mp = Get-MpCmdPath
        if (-not $mp) {
            Write-Output "✘ MpCmdRun.exe not found."
            break
        }

        try {
            Write-Output "↻ Removing all definitions (repair) ..."
            & $mp -RemoveDefinitions -All | Out-String | Write-Output
        } catch {
            Write-Output "✘ Failed to remove definitions: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        }

        try {
            Write-Output "↻ Updating signatures ..."
            Update-MpSignature -Er
```

#### Re-register built-in Windows apps  
`repair-built-in-apps` · admin

```powershell
Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register (Join-Path $package.InstallLocation 'AppxManifest.xml') -ErrorAction Stop
```

#### Setup preflight  
`setup-preflight` · admin

> Checks for a pending restart, critically low disk space and other common setup problems before a recipe changes the PC.

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# This action is deliberately read-only. Hard blockers fail the recipe;
# things that may be perfectly normal on some PCs are reported as warnings.
$blockers = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
$warnings = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

function Write-CheckResult([string]$State, [string]$Message) {
    Write-Output ("[{0}] {1}" -f $State, $Message)
}

function Test-Administrator {
    $identity = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
    $principal = [Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]::new($identity)
    return $principal.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
}

function Get-PendingRestartReasons {
    $reasons = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

    if (Test-Path 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Component Based Servicing\RebootPending') {
        $reasons.Add('Component Based Servicing')
    }
    if (Test-Path 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate\Auto Update\RebootRequired') {
        $reasons.Add('Windows Update')
    }

    $sessionManager = Get-ItemProperty -LiteralPath 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager' -Name PendingFileRenameOperations -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    $pendingFileOperations = @($sessionManager.PendingFileRenameOperations) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) }
    if ($pendingFileOperations.Count -gt 0) {
        $reasons.Add('pending file operations')
    }

    $activeName = (Get-ItemProperty -LiteralPath 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\ComputerName\ActiveComputerName' -Name ComputerName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ComputerName
    $configuredName = (Get-ItemProperty -LiteralPath 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\ComputerName\ComputerName' -Name ComputerName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ComputerName
    if ($activeName -and $configuredName -and $activeName -ne $configuredName) {
        $reasons.Add('pending computer rename')
    }

    return $reasons
}
```
